    “Since when do you smoke?” Lena asked and motioned to the polished wood that Lillian tucked into a bag out of sight.


    “You know fine well this isn’t for me,” Lillian huffed and drew her daughter a look that softened as she caught sight of the mischievous dimples on Lena’s cheeks. “Your father would have enjoyed this, and I’m sure Bernardo will, too.”


    Lena squinted in suspicion over her mother’s behavior and ushered the girls along to purchase other gifts for their grandfather. Andy chose a box of expensive chocolates, Sophia picked out a tie in Bernardo’s style, and Natty selected a giant stuffed walrus.


    “He has a big moustache like abuelo!” Natty touched the bushy whiskers and hugged him to her chest.


    With all of their purchases, Lena herded her family into a private car and their driver took them through the city to Bernardo’s ultra-modern “palacio” – his second home in Mexico, and the one he spent the most living in throughout the year.


    Lillian spent the whole time in the car fluffing her hair and fixing her make-up, and Natty sang off-key to her walrus about his moustache.


    It relieved some of Lena’s worry, and Kara’s hand on her knee took care of the rest. The driver paused at the gate outside Bernardo’s home and Lena entered a security key for access.


    Up the beautifully laid stone driveway was a fountain, and behind it was an architectural marvel of glass and stone. Kara stepped out of the vehicle first and assisted Lillian in getting out. The girls went next, and Lena continued to sit in the same spot as she realized how much she dreaded the chance of encountering Andrea before she was ready.


    She still hadn’t told Sophia about what happened or why Andrea was in Mexico during spring break. The plan was to have a conversation with Andrea first, and it wouldn’t include their daughters.


    Her stomach churned as Kara gave her a hand and she exited the car. She approached the front steps and midway caught a whiff of strange new omega pheromones.


    Kara caught her eye and the private smile she shared coincided with the way her eyes moved towards Sophia.


    The talk Kara had with their middle child must have inspired her to ditch the fancy scent blocker she had been using rather religiously since presenting.


    Lena’s brows came together in awe and Kara leaned closer to confide in a whisper, “I think telling her friend Alison gave her a new perspective on things.”


    “Is it wrong that every time you do something wonderfully parental it gets me hot?” Lena murmured under her breath.


    Their flirtatious pheromones were light enough to fade with the breeze, but the heat between them simmered on as Kara took the lead to walk Lena up the path. They reached the door first, and Kara rang the bell and then stepped back respectfully so that Lena was positioned in front to greet Bernardo.


    He must have seen them on the camera, because the door swung open not two seconds later and the surprise on his face looked more delighted than shocked.


    “Abuelo, mire, he’s just like you!” Natty blurted out before the adults could greet one another. She rushed out of Lillian’s grasp and straight to her grandfather with the walrus that was almost as big as her.


    Natty giggled when he scooped her up to pinch her cheeks.


    “How have you grown already? You’re going to be as tall as Sophia before I know it.” Bernardo laughed and set Natty down so that she could run into his extravagant home.


    “I would have called before dropping by, but it would have made for a poor surprise.” Lena muttered, her smile short lived but genuine. She took a shaky breath as Bernardo regarded her curiously and then sighed when he stepped back to welcome them all inside.


    “Phone calls are for strangers. You’re my family. You can drop by any time. You know that.” Bernado’s lips twitched subtly when he noticed Kara, and he drew himself to his full height as if perplexed to see her standing in his home. “I must be out of touch with the younger generation. I never would have thought to bring a nanny on vacation.”


    Sophia snorted like she thought her grandfather was joking, and Andy halted midstride to glance at Kara and work out the situation. She was quick to put two and two together, and her eyes widened before falling into a squint. “Uh, Kara’s not our nanny. She’s family.”


    The subtle fierceness of that statement took them all by surprise, but none more than Kara, who looked at Andy with emotion in her eyes.

    The pride that came from Kara wasn’t as strong as the outpouring of love and she stood taller and held out her hand to formally introduce herself. “Mr. Rojas, it’s so nice to meet you again. I’m Kara, Lena’s mate.”


    Lena sucked in a deep breath as she noted Bernardo’s shock. “We have a lot to discuss.”


    “We’ll be in the game room if anyone needs us,” Andy announced, catching wind of the tension she created. She hoisted Natty onto her hip and guided Sophia down the hall with a firm hand on her back.


    Sophia attempted to shrug her older sister off, but Andy glared at her in warning.


    Lillian stepped closer to pass off the gilded box of cigars to Bernardo. She made brief but flirtatious eye contact. “It’s been a long time, and I look forward to getting re-acquainted later. For now, I’ll join my granddaughters.”


    Left alone to handle the situation she traveled to Mexico to resolve, Lena clutched Kara’s hand and followed Bernardo into another room.


    “I divorced Andrea years ago,” Lena prefaced and shied away from any possible judgment she might have seen on Bernardo’s face. “I got pregnant with Natty after our marriage was long over. I know how that sounds, and I also know I shouldn’t have lied to you about Kara. Andrea asked us both to keep our relationship a secret. All of this time, I just assumed that Andrea would confide in you. I’m so sorry—”


    Bernardo settled down on his sofa and gestured to them both to sit. “Siéntense, por favor. You are not to blame for any of this, cariño. Okay, you should have been honest, but Andrea was the one who deliberately deceived me. Even now, she weaves tales and tells me that you will have more children together.”


    Kara winced at the revelation and stiffened in her seat. The pungent reek of her anger filled the room like smoke, and she didn’t censor herself as she gritted out, “The only children Lena will be having in the future are mine. Your daughter lost that right when she decided her ego was more important than her marriage.”


    Bernardo peered over at Kara with a glimmer of respect in his eyes. “And how did her ego get the best of her?”


    Lena folded her hands in her lap and stared down at them as she cut in to answer that question. “Andrea was unfaithful to me. Not just in the later years of our marriage, but from the very beginning.”


    That news must have rocked the entire foundation of what Bernardo believed about his daughter. He hunched forward, placing his hands at the back of his neck. “Andrea must explain this behavior to me. She must account for it, because this is not the Rojas way. I raised her to be loyal to family, and what familial bond is more important than the relationship between an alpha and omega?”


    “None,” Kara enunciated sharply, jutting her chin and proving her own values by tightening her grip on Lena’s hand. “Except for the bond we have with our children. That’s why we’re in Mexico.”


    “Andrea hasn’t been responding to any of my calls or texts, and the girls are expecting to spend their spring break with her, because it’s tradition.” Lena expected Bernardo to judge her for moving on with her life, but still pressed on to explain what she wanted. “I can tolerate her cold shoulder, but I won’t allow her to subject our daughters to that. She told us she was going to Mexico to visit her mother’s grave, and I haven’t heard from her since.”


    Bernardo rubbed at his moustache in thought and took out his phone. He stood up without mentioning what he was doing and wandered around as he waited for Andrea to pick up his call.


    “Papi, cómo estás?” Andrea spoke loudly enough to be heard despite the fact that Bernardo was standing several steps away.


    “Muy mal, mija.” Bernardo responded in a voice that was deep, rumbling, and troubled. “I suggest you finish your business and return here. We need to talk.”

    Chapter 25

    Chapter Notes

    Lena didn’t say a word as Bernardo returned to his seat, though she did bow her head as panic tightened her chest. Kara picked up on her dread and did her best to console her with her pheromones, and Lena was grateful for that. In all her years with Andrea, she had always held her father-in-law's respect. It disturbed her to feel like that might be crumbling in the wake of Bernardo finding out about the seeds of deceit his daughter had sown.

    Andrea would arrive within the hour, and the prospect of facing her ex had Lena curling in on herself before she realized it was happening.  It stemmed from years of emotional abuse and her misplaced sense of failure that made her feel half the size.


    Bernardo’s sharp eyes narrowed in on Lena’s behavior and then he walked over to speak with Kara. “I want you to know that I will always think of Lena as a daughter, divorce or not, and that leaves me with questions for you. It’s a rare alpha who chooses an omega who has been claimed before. Can you look me in the eye and tell me you’re capable of raising and loving another alpha’s children?”


    Kara sat forward to meet Bernardo’s intensity head on. “I am.”


    Lena handled business negotiations all the time, though none were as volatile as the one that played out in front of her.


    Both Bernardo and Kara seemed ready to fiercely protect her, and Lena’s heart was in her throat because of it.


    “Why is that?” Bernardo pressed, his old school views of traditional alpha roles completely tested as he looked to Kara. “Blood isn’t a bond that can be broken. Andrea is their sire. She will always have a place in their lives.”


    Kara kept her head held high and didn’t once flinch at his stance. “As she should. I’m not a replacement for Andrea, but I will be an active parent to the girls.”


    Bernardo was hard to read as he drew upon all his experience as a CEO to stare at Kara without giving away his true feelings. He kept his tone firm as he grilled Kara, and in a lot of ways it reminded Lena of her own father and how protective he had been when still alive. “And you’re prepared for that? To be in each other's lives for the children no matter what?”


    It went without saying what Bernardo was implying. That Andrea and Kara would have to co-exist for the rest of their lives, regardless of how they hated one another.


    Lena had no doubt that Kara could put aside her differences for the benefit of the girls, but she didn’t trust that Andrea would.


    “The kids will always come first. I knew that before I asked Lena to date me.” Kara asserted with a conviction that rendered Bernardo speechless.


    He steepled his fingers thoughtfully. There was a touch of respect to his pheromones, faint but promising. “Family matters to you, even if it’s not one you played a part in creating. That is unusual for an alpha.”


    Kara must have detected the change in him, since she squared her shoulders and postured fully. “Family is what we make it. I lost my parents when I was very young. I spent years in the foster system, so I know what it’s like to have no one. Just as I gave up hope, a family took me in. I might not share biology with my sister, Mr. Rojas, or my mom, but they are my family, and so are your granddaughters.”


    Lena admired her mate’s strength, and the way Kara showed it without arrogance or by trying to dominate the conversation, but instead by being unapologetically vulnerable.


    She slipped her hand into Kara’s, and stroked her thumb while Bernardo took his time reading the emotion on her face.


    The silence between them was poignant and Lena refused to intrude on it.


    Bernardo was the first to end it, with a line of questioning that hit at other serious concerns any father might have when a new relationship is unveiled. “What is it that you do for a living, Kara?”


    Lena witnessed her mate translate that in her mind with the way Kara’s jaw tensed. 


    What are you bringing to this relationship and how are you providing for the family?


    Business was a touchy subject for anyone, but in the Rojas family it was both a duty and a legacy. That was one thing other than their children that Lena and Andrea truly shared in common. They were both expected to follow in their family’s footsteps and to excel in expanding their fortune, the pressures of which fell heaviest on Andrea as she tried to prove herself to Bernardo.


    Given the grief over Kara’s deal with Siobhan being a lie, Lena wouldn’t have been surprised if Kara informed Bernardo of how Andrea tried to sabotage her livelihood. But Kara was a better alpha than her ex and never brought Andrea into it.


    “I own a pool cleaning business,” Kara admitted and kept to the kind of facts that Bernardo would care about. “I built it from the ground up, and now I have several trusted teams of people who meet my high standards of service.”


    “So you’re ambitious, driven and not afraid of failure. Those are good qualities to have as an alpha.” Bernardo seemed relieved to discover that Kara was self-made, though whether or not he respected her line of work was difficult to gauge.


    He didn’t insult their relationship by asking if Kara loved her, because it was evident given the claims on Lena’s neck.


    This gave Kara a chance to turn things around, and Bernardo appeared surprised by how she seized the opportunity after he paused his interrogation.


    “You said Lena will always be your daughter. Does that mean any future children she has will be welcome here with the girls, or will they be treated differently from their siblings?”


    Lena held her breath at Kara’s fearlessness to ask a question that hadn’t even entered her own mind. She wanted to have several more children with Kara, but this was the first time she was forced to consider that they might not be welcome to join the girls in Mexico, or anywhere else Bernardo considered a family gathering.


    Bernardo blinked at the direct way Kara addressed it, and then his eyes fell to Lena as though he saw her in a different light. For a fleeting instant, he lost his stoic facade and his eyes shined with something familiar. It was gone in an instant, and he turned to Kara with the same steel in his voice as he rasped, “Family is family. Any pups you have are of course welcome here.”


    “So I have your word?” Kara showed the true colors of her alpha as she ensured that their daughters would never be deprived of making memories with their future siblings, or pitted against each other.


    Bernardo held his hand out as if it was as good as any legal document and shook Kara’s with a force that jerked her forward. “On my wife’s grave.”


    The touching moment brought a flood of tears to Lena’s eyes. Though she tried to hold them back, she failed miserably and sniffled into her hand. Her hormonal state was taking a toll on her, and while Kara turned with concern to wipe at her cheek, Bernardo stood up to pull Lena into his arms.


    “Do not cry, Lena,” Bernardo soothed and pulled a handkerchief from his pocket to give her. “You should have known a divorce wouldn’t change anything, eh? I am always here for you and the girls.”


    Lena looked down at the fine silk in her hand and patted it against her eyes. She subdued the soft cry in her throat and breathed in the sweet relief of having Bernardo’s love and support.


    It might not have been the best scene for Andrea to witness upon her arrival. None of them noticed her at first, and Andrea scoffed at the sight of them embracing.


    “So, this is your revenge? You come to my father’s house and sob on his shoulder so he’ll believe you’re the innocent party in all of this?” Andrea slipped her arms over her chest and flared her nostrils in outrage.


    The stand-off between them could have gone on for ages if Bernardo hadn’t been standing right behind Lena. He stepped in front of her before Kara had the chance.


    Bernardo expanded his chest with a slow inhale and held back nothing in his criticism of his daughter. “Lena isn’t the one who has been deceitful. You led me to believe that you were still married and expecting to have more children. Meanwhile, you’ve been divorced for years, and during your marriage, you were disloyal to your wife. I didn’t raise you to behave that way.”


    Andrea snorted at his calm speech and picked her words to do the maximum amount of damage. “You hardly raised me at all. You sent me to boarding school when I was grieving my mother’s death so you could travel all over the world with other omegas.”

    “No, I gave you the education your mother wanted you to have,” Bernardo snapped, his teeth briefly bared as pain flashed across his features. “I honored her wishes–”


    “Is that what you tell yourself? That you honored her by shipping me to America so you could sleep with omegas half her age?” Andrea’s scorn came out as a hiss and her lip curled in disdain for her father.


    Lena gagged on the scent of her ex’s disgust and blindly reached for Kara to curl herself into the safety of her arms. She had witnessed her fair share of bitter arguments over the years between Andrea and her father, but not once had her ex made such accusations to Bernardo’s face.


    “I spent a fortune giving you the best life I could and somehow you’re still just an ignorant child.” Bernardo stared at his daughter in disbelief and tempered his anger by treating Andrea as though she were throwing a tantrum.


    The pressure of decades worth of resentment and festering trauma finally reached a breaking point inside of Andrea that forced it to burst out. She sneered at her father as she threw attacks at him in the form of questions. “Was she even in the ground before you started sleeping with half the cleaning staff, or did you help send her to an early grave by breaking her heart?”


    Lena had long since been accustomed to Andrea weaponizing every insecurity she had, but it still left her reeling to witness it happen to Bernardo. The atmosphere thickened in the room, cold and overbearing like they were trapped beneath storm clouds.


    Bernardo’s voice was thunderous as he walked toward Andrea, his pride and pain etched into his brow as he raged, “How dare you walk in here and vilify me when you’ve made a mockery of Lena and your family! You destroyed your marriage, and over what?”


    “Where do you think I learned it from?” Andrea seethed in return, not once flinching away from the conflict. “Even now you don’t see the lessons you taught me, do you?”


    “I loved your mother–”


    “So much that you had to fuck my tutor when I spent my first vacation with you after mom died?” Andrea’s sharp tongue sliced through Bernardo’s posturing, and she tossed her hand up as if being struck with an epiphany. “No, wait, you loved her so much that’s why every time I saw you there was a new trophy on your arm. I guess I should be thanking you, right? Since you showed me that alphas aren’t equipped to love anyone except themselves.”


    Kara cautiously dropped her hand to cover Lena’s stomach and eased them out of the way as Bernardo’s pheromones battled his daughter’s furious perfume.


    The astringent scent burned Lena’s lungs, and though none of it was aimed at her, she experienced the awful sensation of her omega begging forgiveness. Kara put a stop to that by enveloping her in a protective musk to block out the worst of it, and Lena nosed into her mate’s shirt to calm her nausea.


    “Let me tell you something,” Bernardo ranted and advanced on Andrea without care as to who overheard their fight. “Your mother is the only omega I have ever loved, and the only one I ever will. The women I share my life with know they have no place in my heart. They are content to be pretty distractions because I set them on a path to live good lives. I am honest with them that I will never allow myself the chance to feel anything stronger than fondness. Anything more would be a betrayal to your mother.”


    Andrea’s defenses dropped at the realization that Bernardo wasn’t a cheater, or the heartless bastard that she believed him to be. The uninhibited scent of her despair was pungent enough to startle them all, and then she hid it with misplaced anger that should have been directed at herself.


    “How noble of you to find a way to justify your shitty behavior. What wisdom did you think you were imparting as you cycled through omegas faster than suits?” The venom in Andrea’s voice wasn’t as effective with the warble of her chin.


    For a sickening instant, Lena saw the young woman she had once loved beneath the layers of bullshit — the deep regret from every selfish action she had taken and how irrevocably damaged she became in the process.


    Anguish threatened to spill down Andrea’s cheeks, though Bernardo showed his daughter no mercy as he called out her detestable actions.


    “So, this is how you rationalize your infidelity? You blame me while trying to emulate who you think I am?” Bernardo scoffed, affronted by Andrea’s lack of humility for how she wrecked her own marriage. “All this time I thought you strived to be an alpha worthy of an omega like Lena, but it’s clear to me that you’ve never understood the value of real love. This is why she found someone who does.”


    Whatever breakthrough Andrea might have been on the cusp of having was tarnished by the fiery outrage of her father acknowledging Kara and Lena’s relationship. She drew herself up to her full height to shout, “Are you seriously giving them your fucking blessing in the middle of our argument? Have they even told you that they’re planning to steal my children?”


    Lena wasn’t prepared to be caught in the middle of their wrath and gaped in shock at Andrea’s deflection. She stared at her ex with wounded, large eyes and uselessly tried to make her tongue work.


    “Is this true, Lena?” Bernardo asked, his voice still hoarse from all his yelling.



    “No, Mr. Rojas, it isn’t,” Kara grunted and stepped in to set matters straight. “Andrea’s skipping the part where she told Lena to take full custody–”



    “After Kara punched me and I feared for my safety,” Andrea spat, resembling a child who was trying to tattle first. “I was under duress and not in my right mind.”


    Bernardo’s parental instinct still kicked in despite the ongoing conflict and he squinted at Kara like a father filled with disappointment. “You hit my daughter?”


    “Yeah, and I’m about to do it again,” Kara threatened with a snarl as she glared at Andrea for trying to twist the narrative to her advantage.


    Lena gripped at her mate’s wrist to stop her from moving and shook her head as she addressed Bernardo. “We’re not filing for full custody. Kara is in the process of becoming their legal guardian, but we would never try to strip Andrea of her parental rights. Andrea ran off after we discovered that she slept with Kara’s friend to spy on our relationship. She also tried to sabotage Kara’s business.”


    “Hey, Nia loved every second of my attention, and it’s not my fault I exposed your rebound as an idiot who honestly thought that being a pool cleaner gave her the credentials to work as an engineer.” Andrea frothed at the corners of her mouth and the buttons on her suit jacket strained from her posturing.


    “Oh, I’m stupid?” Kara snarled, her biceps threatening the integrity of her t-shirt as she turned to Andrea like she might just throttle her in front of Bernardo. “That’s funny, I don’t remember walking out on my omega and abandoning my kids.”


    Kara’s remark was the verbal equivalent of a matador waving a red cape and it provoked Andrea just the same. She stalked forward with flared nostrils and growled in Kara’s face, “They’re mine, not yours, and they will never see you as family.”


    Lena knew what Kara was about to say just from the way she raised her chin, and she anticipated that all hell would break loose.


    “They already do,” Kara revealed, though it was less of a brag and more of a simple fact that she used to push Andrea out of her personal space. She advanced forward with steel in her spine and towered over Andrea in contempt. “Maybe if your head wasn’t so far up your own entitled ass, you would see that. We’ve spent weeks trying to reach you, and instead of thinking of the kids, you put yourself first again.”


    Andrea brought her hands up like she might shove Kara, then reconsidered as she vehemently spat, “Don’t stand there and try to berate me on what you think a parent should be. You have no idea what it takes to raise a family. While you play house, I’m the one out here working so that my daughters can have everything they want in life.”


    “Yeah, I’m sure an absentee sire is top of their list. Do you even know who Sophia’s friends are? Any idea what instrument Andy wants to learn first? Can you name Natty’s favorite stuffed animals?” Kara fired back with the full expectation that Andrea would know none of the answers.


    Kara smirked at the way Andrea blinked as she tried to recall any shred of information.


    “No? You have no clue who your children are, because you’re never there to find out.”


    The prospect of violence pushed Lena forward as she saw her ex-wife’s hand curl into a fist, and she tried to dampen the fire of her anger with the scent of her omega pleading for everyone to calm down. “What you see as frivolities are the things that will stick with them forever, Andrea. No amount of money you earn will compensate for that, but you can still turn things around. It’s not too late.”


    Andrea scoffed at Lena’s attempt at reconciliation and drew Kara a hateful look as she hissed, “Does this make you feel like an alpha? Coming to my father’s home to attack me with Lena on your arm?”


    “I’m not the one who needs an audience to perform in front of, Andrea. I’m here because it was my idea to bring the girls to Mexico to spend time with their ungrateful sire.” The animosity of Kara’s words should have warned Andrea to stop, but it had the reverse effect.


    Instead of considering how she had failed so far as a parent, Andrea doubled down on her audacity. “I don’t care how many bites you leave on Lena’s neck. My teeth were on her skin first and it’s my seed she carried–”


    Bernardo reached his limit for Andrea’s volatile personality and intervened before her rant could continue. “Enough. What kind of alpha are you, putting all of this stress onto Lena’s shoulders?” He motioned with his hand as if to inform his daughter of Lena’s condition, though Andrea seemed blind to it.


    If not for Kara’s closeness, Lena might have staggered as the fear of Andrea finding out she was pregnant hit her. She wasn’t sure she was ready for that conversation, and judging from the way Kara bristled, she imagined her mate wasn’t, either.


    Andrea’s focus switched onto her father and she frowned at him in disbelief. “Oh, you want to talk about stress, now? Where was that concern when you pushed me out of the house and into Obsidian North before I’d even graduated from college?”


    “That was different. I was preparing you for greatness, to lead as an alpha–”


    “You were forcing me into your shoes, no matter the cost to my own mental health,” Andrea sputtered with an incredulous laugh. “Is it any wonder I sought a way to alleviate it when you were crushing me under the weight of your ambition?”


    Lena choked on air as she gaped at Andrea and forgot about the risks to her health as her blood pressure spiked. “Did you honestly just say you had multiple affairs because you were overworked?”


    “Don’t act like you wouldn’t have done the same if the opportunity arose,” Andrea dismissively stated with a purse of her lips. “I saw your eyes wander.”


    Lena recoiled at the implication and then surged forward only for Kara to catch her about the waist to hold her back. “Fuck you, Andrea–”


    “You have, hundreds of times,” Andrea gloated straight to Kara’s face, as if that was all that mattered.


    “There’s a difference between having eyes and sticking it in everything that moves,” Kara snarled in defense and positioned herself so that Lena was hidden from Andrea.


    “I’m not going to be shamed for sharing a bed with you when we were married,” Lena insisted, albeit weakly as she fought her own remorse for being stupid and falling for all of Andrea’s lies at the time.


    Andrea’s smug grin was all for show, though her ego seemed bigger than ever. “I’m not trying to shame you. I’m just making it clear that even without a ring, my history with you will outlast this fling with her.”


    Bernardo had a grave look on his face as he spoke to his daughter. “If this is how you behave, I see now why Kara knocked you on your ass. If anyone spoke to your mother like that when she was carrying you, I’d have done much worse.”


    “Of course you’d defend that asshole, she’s–” Andrea’s throat closed over as her father’s words fully registered and she gawked at Lena like she had just been told her life was over.


    Bernardo ignored his daughter in favor of escorting Lena into a chair, his hushed words filled with comfort and love. “Sit down, Lena. All of this yelling isn’t good for you.”


    “How long?” Andrea rasped, her voice barely above a whisper as the color drained from her face.


    “That’s none of your business, and if you tell anyone before we get the chance…” Kara’s threat remained open-ended, and even Bernardo seemed to approve as he glared at his daughter disapprovingly.


    The news sucked the fight right out of Andrea, and she sank into a chair utterly defeated. She looked shell-shocked, as if the entire concept of Lena and Kara’s relationship had been meaningless up until now—a phase that she thought she could withstand in order to win Lena back. With a new pup on the way, that fantasy was over, and the reality of what Andrea truly lost was all that remained.


    Bernardo handled the matter with softness and grace. “This situation has not been a healthy one, and for the sake of the children, it’s imperative that we find a way to progress as a family. That means no more interfering in their relationship, Andrea, or I’ll cut you from my will.”


    That threat must have seemed inconsequential when compared to all else that took place. Andrea hunched forward in her seat, making eye contact with no one. She breathed heavier and gathered herself up to flee through the side door. It would have been a good escape route if all three of their kids weren’t waiting right behind it with Lillian, who backed up and attempted to look innocent.


    “We thought we heard voices in here.” Lillian shrugged as her astute eyes landed on Andrea. “Your voice certainly does travel through walls and down halls, but we couldn’t quite make out the conversation.”


    “Mommy!” Natty latched onto Andrea’s legs, oblivious to the tension of the adults in the room. “I have a new friend for Frederico. Mama bought him for me. His name is Guillermo.”


    Sophia lunged into her mother’s arms, and Andrea looked down at her in blatant shock as she inhaled omega pheromones.


    Andy stood more than two feet away, posturing and glaring at her namesake. “Did you miss us?”


    “I-yes–” Andrea wheezed, so caught off guard by the consecutive changes in her life that her usual commanding presence was subdued. She awkwardly placed her hand on Sophia’s shoulder and didn’t chastise Natty as the little one creased her pants by clinging to her knees.

    Lena was inclined to believe they were late as she caught the miserable look on Andrea’s face. She flattened her dress against her thighs so she could march over to her ex. Natty reached for her, and Lena tried to soothe her baby by wiping the wisps of hair out of her face.


    “Why is Natty screaming, and where is Sophia?” Lena asked.


    “I’d forgotten the chaos that came with family plans,” Andrea griped and handed Natty off to Lena with the clear expectation that she would fix the situation for her. “I guess my nostalgia erased all of the worst parts about it. Natalia refused her breakfast, and I told her she has to eat something or we’re not going anywhere.”


    “You thought tough love would help?” Lena hissed through her teeth and propped Natty on her hip to comfort her. She rubbed her palm in semi-circles over the little one’s back while Natty hiccupped between sobs. “Did you even bother to ask her why she doesn’t want to eat?”


    “Of course I did,” Andrea informed her snidely, as though she held Lena personally responsible for Natty’s unreasonable behavior. “She thinks we’re going to be late, and she wants to give her pancakes to the mermaids. Sophia tried to share her bowl of fruit and she ended up wearing it when Natty pitched a fit.”


    It surprised Lena that Sophia had been the one to persuade Natty to have breakfast, and she smiled in spite of the circumstances. “Where is Sophia now?”


    “Probably still showering and cursing Andy while she’s at it,” Andrea sighed heavily and directed her frown at their eldest daughter. “Someone found the whole thing funny, and Sophia decided the best course of action was revenge.”


    “Tell me they didn’t,” Lena groaned in distress and pinched the bridge of her nose to fight the oncoming headache. She imagined the food fight before Andrea even mentioned it, and wondered why, out of all their days at the resort, things had to go wrong now.


    “You remember the Easter when Sophia was six and Andy laughed because she covered herself in chocolate?” Disgust curled Andrea’s lips and she mindlessly wiped at her business suit to rid herself of the messy memory. “Well, it was worse. Sophia flung the entire platter of fruit at Andy, and all hell broke loose because Andy tossed a bunch of greasy bacon right back at her.”

    “Lena, and just where were you when we were on the verge of World War 3?” Lillian demanded with an air of authority that shouldn’t have worked on someone Lena’s age.


    “Getting ready for the apparently long day ahead of us,” Lena retorted with the perfect poker face. She swept away from Andrea before her ex could make a comment about what they had been doing, and she tried to communicate with Kara through scent alone.


    Her mate was fortunately well tuned to her needs, and Lena smiled in gratitude the moment Kara abandoned her plate of food to escort her over to the buffet. The problem was that Lillian and Andrea trailed after her.


    Natty thrashed in Lillian’s arms and screeched like a tiny pterodactyl.


    “I don’t want to miss the mermaids!” Natty wailed with tears streaming down her cheeks and snot bubbling at her nose.


    Andrea stopped mid stride and walked off in appalled silence the moment she saw the state of their youngest child.


    Lena knew the neat freak in her ex was close to snapping, and part of her wanted to hand Natty back to Andrea and force her to parent.


    Kara didn’t need to be asked and gathered Natty from Lillian as though it was her duty to comfort their kid.


    “Aww, hey, it’s okay, the mermaids are still having breakfast, too,” Kara explained and carefully wiped at Natty’s face with the soft cuff of her button down shirt. “I bet they would want you to have a full tummy when you see them so you don’t get tired. Why don’t we make a plate together?”

    Even though Lena braced herself for the worst possible reaction, she still balked at the confident way her mother asserted, “You should skip the pastries this morning and have salad instead. Kara’s claim is on your throat, but there isn’t a ring on your finger yet. I would be doing you a disservice if I didn’t encourage you to keep your figure.”

    The scoff came out of her with enough force to draw Kara’s attention, and Lena hurried to confront her mother without comprehending the gift they had been given. “Are you seriously telling me to watch my weight while we’re on vacation?”


    “All I’m saying is that the dress you’re wearing looks a little snug around your middle,” Lillian huffed with the good grace to look embarrassed. She peered at the fabric that did indeed show off the slight roundness to Lena’s stomach and pursed her lips as if truly concerned that Kara might be swayed by an extra pound or two.


    Lena couldn’t exactly blame her mother, given Andrea’s tendencies to wander during their relationship, but it still stung to hear Lillian say such a thing.


    “Uh—Lena—what did I miss?” Kara asked from the sidelines where she hovered with a plate of food. Natty chewed glumly on a banana, oblivious to the tension between the adults.

She set her breakfast aside to lace her fingers through Lena’s and stared down at her with enough adoration to make Lillian blush. “Everyone’s body changes with time. It doesn’t mean I’ll love Lena’s any less, and I sure hope she feels the same way about me.”

    “Is there some kind problem between you and Kara?” Sophia asked with a unique and adept talent for clocking true tensions in people.


    Lena’s sensitivity was evident on her face, and she worried that Sophia would over analyze the conversation she heard if she didn’t explain. At the same time, Lena couldn’t mention that she was pregnant or bring up the texts that she had seen on Kara’s phone that instilled some anxiety in her.


    “It’s nothing,” Lena insisted and locked eyes with their middle child. “Your grandmother was just concerned that I was over indulging and that Kara would take issue with that. Kara loves me no matter what I look like. Maybe I have put on a little weight since we’ve been here. So what? The food is just that good.”


    “It’s not that good,” Sophia sniffed and ran a thick toothed comb through her wet hair. She applied some gel to achieve a slicked-back look more common among alphas. “The vegetarian options could be better, but Grandma shouldn’t body-shame you.”


    “I wasn’t body-shaming her,” Lillian replied with wide eyes that narrowed as she realized she would have to defend her point diplomatically in front of Sophia. “I admit that I might have overstepped with my remark, but I assure you all, I was coming from a place of love and I truly meant no harm. I’m sorry, Lena. I see how happy you are, and I don’t want anything to change that.”

It was instinct to pull away and seek comfort in the safe haven of Kara’s pheromones, and Lillian fortunately didn’t push it as she extracted herself from the situation with a pained glance towards Kara.


    “We have to go now,” Natty insisted with an elongated whine. It bordered on a fresh sob, and she jerked her little legs like she wanted to run off.


    “On that note,” Lena muttered with a frown and beckoned Sophia closer while Kara tried to placate Natty. “Can you please inform your abuelo and your mom we need to leave now, or the only waterworks we’ll see today will be Natty’s.”


    “This day hasn’t even started and I’m already over it,” Sophia grumbled with a huff and walked off to get away from the impending shrieks of her little sister.


    Lena experienced the smallest twinge of guilt for sharing that sentiment. She drew strength from Kara and the hopeful smile on her mate’s lips and realized she could be kissing them soon if they shared a car without the kids.


    “You’re coming with me,” Lena murmured flirtatiously and linked her arm through Kara’s with the aspiration of stealing her away for some stress relief across the leather seats.


    Lena knew it was a pipe dream the minute Sophia’s voice carried over the wails of Natty, “No way! There’s three cars and I’m not sharing one with her.”


    “Good,” Andy grunted with a dismissive glare at her sister. “Then I don’t have to see your stupid face for a while.”


    “Girls, that’s enough,” Andrea hissed and surprised everyone by showing the initiative to create some distance between them instead of leaving it up to Lena. “Andy will ride with me.”


    Sophia appeared offended by Andrea’s choice, and Andy snorted at the blatant attempt to trap her in a car for forced bonding. “Hard pass, I’ll go with mom.”


    “Lillian and I will take Natalia, so she arrives there first,” Bernardo suavely stated and held out his arms for Natty, who excitedly leapt at her grandfather.


    Andrea still looked pissed off, but she reined in her anger and motioned for Sophia to get in the car while Andy slid herself into the backseat of the last vehicle.


    Kara followed suit, and Lena accompanied her with the tight-lipped resignation that she would have to behave herself for the next twenty minutes. The ride was quiet for the most part with Andy glued to her cell phone the whole way to their destination.


    La Canción de Las Sirenas     took place near the aquarium, and a lot of families were already waiting in line to meet the mermaids. Andrea paid for a special VIP pass and Natty brought along a bunch of drawings to give to her new sea-friends, Dorita, Esperanza and Gisela.


    It looked like peace had been restored in the family, since Sophia was talking to Natty and hyping her up for the experience. One of the mermaid’s helpers walked down the line and handed out beaded necklaces and hats. Lena put on her necklace and caught Kara’s drifting down to her cleavage and the pressed together swells of her tits that peeked out of her too-small demi cups.

    Lena tried not to take too much enjoyment out of the number of times Natty accidentally kicked her sire. She did take count: five so far, and Andrea groaned once, but Natty wouldn’t have been able to see all of the attractions without someone hoisting her up.


    “Mama, can we meet the mermaid with the pink and purple hair?” Natty asked and wrapped her little hand around the collar on Andrea’s blouse.


    “Si, we’re going to meet all of them,” Andrea promised with more excitement than expected of her.

    “Andrea! Cabrón. You told me you didn’t want any kids. I should have known you were a liar. Como todo alfas.”

    Natty gasped and turned her big trusting eyes to Andrea with all the innocent excitement only a child could possess. “Mama, you love mermaids, too?”


    “Love is a very strong word, Natalia. I enjoyed Gisela’s company very much,” Andrea corrected, though not nearly as hushed as she had hoped. Far too late, she figured out how that would come across and held her hand up to placate Gisela with an apology.


    “Idiota!” Gisela snapped in offense and slapped her hand against the water to splash Andrea.


    Some of the spray hit Natty in the face, and it was in that moment she realized the mermaid wasn’t happy to see her the way she had been with the other kids.


    Too young to comprehend that her sire was the reason, Natty’s lip trembled in distress before a warble erupted from her that was loud enough to draw the eyes of the crowd.


    “She huh-hates me!” Natty sobbed between harsh breaths that shook her shoulders.

Remember Ariel? Gisela must have liked your Mom a whole lot. She’s just sad that it didn’t work out between them.”

    The field for archery was out by the tennis courts. The walk tested the integrity of Lena’s dress and its ability to keep her breasts where they belonged. Lena wouldn’t have cared, but a few alphas stopped their games and blatantly ogled her in front of Sophia.

Her mate took up the middle position between the girls, and for a prolonged second, Lena admired the cut of her mate’s strong arms and how effortlessly she raised the bow to test the sight.

She wouldn’t utter such filthy things in front of the kids, but her claim pheromones carried a private and flirtatious scent for Kara to let her know where her mind wandered.

I don’t remember you throwing any shade when our sire dated every single omega in the county. Why is this different? Andy’s defensive attitude formed a giant crater in their day. It forced Lena into being the kind of parent she never wanted to be.
