    She did her best not to snoop in Kara’s bags when her mate vanished from the house for a few hours and came back with items that she stashed in the spare room upstairs.



    Lena had no idea what Kara had in store for them - or what her mate was even doing once they tucked Natty in and Andy had locked herself away in her room for the night.



    She stayed up for as long as she could before exhaustion took over, and woke the next morning to Kara already making breakfast so they could head out as soon as possible.



    “I don’t recall you coming to bed last night,” Lena muttered under her breath with a pout that would devastate Kara upon sight. “If I had known your plans would keep you from me for so long, I wouldn’t have agreed to them.”



    “I wasn’t about to wake you just to say goodnight. You need all the rest you can get.” Kara nuzzled into her claims with a soft rumble. “I made you blueberry pancakes and avocado toast, so you can’t be mad at me.”



    If hunger hadn’t been so pressing, Lena might have exploited the situation for more affection. She helped herself to the delicious breakfast while Kara got Natty ready for their long drive.



    Andy appeared a few minutes later and grabbed a stack of pancakes.



    Thirty minutes later, they all piled into Kara’s truck and headed off to pick up Lillian. Alex and Sam had gotten a head start on their morning on account of having fewer mouths to feed. Lena decided to text Andrea a reminder that she was expected to attend Parents Weekend for Sophia, but she didn’t receive a message back.



    At Natty’s demand, they listened to the Encanto soundtrack for the entire ride and arrived at DC Prep in time to sign Sophia out for lunch. They would spend Friday afternoon and night together and return to the boarding school for the events starting on Saturday morning.



    A lot of cars traveled down the long drive to the exclusive school, and a group of students exited the building to meet up with their families.



    “I texted Sophia and she said we can pick her up out front.” Andy tapped on her phone screen to send a text to her sister. “Ruby is giving Sam and Alex a tour of her room now that she set it all up.”



    Kara pulled the car up to the pick-up location and Lena exited the car with the belief that Sophia would look no different than she had during drop-off.



    Sophia weaved through a crowd of students with Andrea already by her side. She carried a purse and a make-up kit along with a large bag of goodies in an Obsidian Tech tote.



    Lena blinked at her daughter’s full face of powder and shadow. Sophia’s eyelashes curled up to her brow bone and her lipstick was the exact shade that Lena liked to wear.



    “Mom told me I need to clean my face,” Sophia complained and looked to Lena to disagree. “She also bought me an entire bag of Alpha repellent.”



    “Alpha repellent?” Lena frowned and peeked into the Obsidian tote as she threw a questioning glance Andrea’s way.



    “Scent maskers, a whole line of perfume, and three candles to prevent an alpha from ever wanting to step foot in my room. There’s also a few books.” Sophia listed off the items and pulled a questionable looking book out of the bag. “50 Ways to Say No to an Alpha?”



    Lena borrowed the thick volume from her daughter to skim the description on the back. She glanced towards Kara to silently work out her opinion on Andrea’s new and overbearing approach to parenting their omega child.



    “Are you upset?” Lena asked as a smile graced Sophia’s lips.



    “Just about the make-up,” Sophia admitted and retrieved the book from Lena’s hands to tuck back into her bag. “I’m in a relationship now and most of this stuff is useless to me, but mom also bought me a bunch of my favorite snacks.”



    “Wait a minute, you’re in a relationship?” Andrea stressed in horror and glanced around in paranoia at the rest of Sophia’s classmates. “Since when?”



    Sophia flashed a dainty little silver bracelet with charms on her wrist. “Since Alison gave me this after Spring break. Her sire took her to Europe because her mom and step-sire were busy with their restaurant.”



    “Wow, it sounds like a lot of new things have happened since you returned to school. Maybe you can update us while we grab lunch?” Kara’s diplomatic way of handling it helped to diffuse the tension brewing between Andrea and her daughter, though Lena noted her mate’s smile appeared strained.



    None of them were overjoyed by the development between Sophia and Alison, but casting disapproval on the relationship could backfire tremendously. They had to tread with caution, and discussing it at the pick-up point wasn’t ideal.



    “Sure, but only if I get to ride shotgun,” Sophia stipulated with a practiced flutter of her lashes. The thick mascara glued the edges shut and Lena tried not to stare at the globs that were clearly applied to spite Andrea.



    Given how Sophia had spent the majority of her life trying to imitate her sire, Lena could only conclude she had swung the other way to make a statement. If Andrea’s love and affection came with a price, Sophia no longer wanted to pay it.



    Andy showed mercy by keeping her comments on Sophia’s transformation to herself, but she wouldn’t put up with her sister’s attitude. “There’s already five of us in Kara’s truck, so if you want the front seat, you’ll have to go with mom.”



    “Just switch with me then,” Sophia demanded with the kind of entitled attitude that would take time to unlearn.



    “I’m in the backseat. Who do you think is sitting up front?” Andy widened her eyes to mock Sophia’s intelligence and dodged the attack her sister launched with her Obsidian Tote.



    “I could give you my keys if you feel up to driving,” Kara suggested to Lena while the girls were distracted. She pulled the keys out of her pocket but never got to dangle them in front of Lena’s face.



    “And then what? You’ll hitch a ride with Andrea?” Lena asked and gazed beyond Kara to squint at her ex, who was spaced out from her inability to comprehend that Sophia had a girlfriend. “She would sooner drive you into a ditch.”



    Kara’s laugh was virtually soundless and her smile softened with her explanation. “I was thinking I could tag along with Sam and Alex–”



    “No.” Lena cut in with a tone that made it clear that she wouldn’t accept Kara taking a step back, even to appease the kids. “You’re part of this family, and Andrea can suck it up and take my mother.”



    Lillian was still sitting beside Natty in her car seat, oblivious to the unfolding drama her granddaughter was orchestrating.



    “I don’t think Lillian is going to appreciate being trapped in a car with Andrea,” Kara whispered, out of a fear that either of them would hear their tentative plans to pair them together for a short while.



    “There’s nothing my mother loves more than making Andrea uncomfortable and ten minutes isn’t going to kill them.” Lena marched over to inform her ex of what was going to happen.



    Andrea wouldn’t risk causing a scene that would reflect badly on her own self-image and ushered Lillian into the passenger seat of her Benz with a smile so thin it was practically razor sharp.



    Everyone piled back into Kara’s truck, and after a bitter feud of elbows, Andy squeezed in first to give Sophia the window seat. She passed over the pack of Natty’s wet wipes and gestured to Sophia’s face. “You better take that make-up off before Mom loses it. I’ll help you reapply later if you want.”



    Sophia bristled at the implication that she needed any help at all and scrubbed the foundation off of her face in angry swipes. “What do you know about make-up?”



    “That you don’t need to use a whole tube of lipstick in one application, and my eyeliner is flawless,” Andy retorted with an arrogant jut of her chin and settled back to scroll through her phone.



    Lena kept an eye on them in the rear-view mirror and slid her hand onto Kara’s knee as they followed Andrea’s Benz down the road. In an effort to blend their family, they had all agreed to pick one activity for the girls.



    Andrea selected the restaurant for lunch, Kara picked a scenic picnic area near a lake for their baby reveal, and Lena had chosen to end the day with some fun at the bowling alley.



    “I’ll text Sam to let her know where we’re going and we can meet up at the lake after lunch.” Lena squeezed Kara’s thigh before she retrieved her phone from her purse.



    “Why are we going to the lake?” Andy asked with a disgruntled lilt that said she would rather go anywhere else.



    “Because of the beautiful view and because Ruby has never been there.” Kara’s fast answer sounded reasonable and she winked at Lena as Andy shrugged and didn’t argue.



    Finding the restaurant was trickier than Lena thought, and they drove by several kid friendly spots on the way. Andrea chose a five star place called The Silver Spoon, and it looked like a pretentious chance to flex with a date rather than dine with their large family. Lena doubted any of their girls would like the menu. The outside looked upscale and landscaped with a water mill and pond.



    “The portion sizes better not suck here,” Andy sniffed and helped out by unbuckling Natty’s car seat. “If my dessert is nothing but one little smudge on a plate, we’re going for ice cream later.”



    Sophia glanced around at their surroundings and the large sign with the restaurant’s name. “This is the restaurant that Alison’s parents own. Mom just wants to get more information on them.”



    Kara must have sensed the high potential for conflict and hedged it off with a story.



    “Sounds like something Alex did to me when I went on my first date. She got tickets to the same movie because I was nervous and she wanted to have my back.”



    Lena wondered if the situations were as comparable as Kara made them out to be, or if Andrea would embarrass them all.



    In either case, there was no turning back because Andrea and her mother were already inside. Lena noticed her empty Benz parked right up by the entry.



    “Since this is Alison’s parents’ restaurant, I’m sure we can expect a good meal.” Lena raised her eyebrows at her kids and clapped her hands together. “Let’s go. No doubt your grandmother has ordered cocktails and appetizers by now.”



    They shuffled into the restaurant with Kara leading the way carrying Natty on her hip, and Lena lagging behind with their irritable teens.



    As predicted, the inside of The Silver Spoon was not the least compatible with family dining, and Lena realized they were seated at one of the few long tables.



    Since she stayed awake singing during the drive, Natty was tired and rubbing her eyes. “I want chicken nuggets like Kara makes them. With the dinosaurs.”



    “They don’t have those here. You can try quail.” Andrea put out her arms to take their youngest child, but Natty squirmed fussily and pressed her face into Kara’s neck.



    With no choice but to give up, Andrea pinched her lips and glanced at their other two girls.



    “I need to tell Alison where we’re eating lunch.” Sophia sat down and pulled out her phone to take a selfie, which she texted to someone named My heart.



    Lillian sipped a large sunset orange beverage out of a glass that was decorated with colorful sugar. “Thankfully the cocktails here are strong. I’ll be sampling several.”



    Andrea unfolded her napkin in her lap and gave them all a wild-eyed look of desperation as Sophia snapped another selfie. “I ordered for everyone. For lunch, it’s a single menu with locally-sourced farm-to-table food.”



    Lena had never seen her ex so uncomfortable, and it would have been more enjoyable if she wasn’t also disturbed by Sophia’s new behaviors. Beside her, Kara looked equally unnerved and her smile tightened even more with each message that pinged on their daughter’s phone.



    “So, give us the run down on the whole Alison situation,” Andy prompted and then became distracted as the waitstaff appeared with a tiny plate of food for each of them. She grabbed the bite of food and ate it so she could get back to the business of asking questions. “I thought she was interested in someone else?”



    “She was,” Sophia confirmed and reached for her fork to gather up the purée and spinach pastry on her vegetarian plate. “But after I told her I’m an omega, and I stopped wearing my perfume masker all of the time, Alison realized that her feelings for me are much stronger. By the way, I want to have a party for presenting. I was thinking it could be at the same place where we had Andy’s and I could invite my friends back to the house afterwards. We can have a pool party and everyone can sleep over.”



    In an organized fashion, Sophia whipped out her tablet to share a presentation with a list of items to purchase, a budget that factored in the event space for the party, and a schedule of events.



    “Which weekend is this happening?” Andy leaned into her sister’s space to check the screen for the date. “Oh good. I’ll be literally anywhere else.”



    Sophia rolled her eyes and handed the tablet over to Lena. “Kara, can you help me with everything? So far this year, there’s been a bunch of omegas in my grade who have presented. I’ve heard their parties were mid. I want the alphas to actually have a good time at my party.”



    “You want my help?” Kara asked in surprise and grabbed for ice water to fix her throat. “I’d be honored to handle the set up with you.”



    Sophia squealed in a high-pitched and ear damaging way. “I was thinking we could get one of those gigantic unicorn floats and we could turn the pool house into a tropical paradise with plants and flowers. Maybe we could even make our own macrame plant holders.”



    “Alphas will love using those as sling shots,” Andy mocked, not letting up on her playful criticism.



    The waitstaff delivered the next dish, and while Natty happily picked at the first one, she wrinkled her nose at the salad course. She had learned through the years of having Andrea as a parent to try any meal put down in front of her, but she made a lot of funny faces while doing it.



    Between being over tired and hungry, Natty’s current look forecasted trouble. Lena moved the little one onto her lap and attempted to pick apart the salad.



    “I don’t like it here,” Natty whined and slumped forward in a dramatic, withered posture.



    “Just eat your salad,” Sophia demanded, throwing a paranoid glance towards the kitchen. She picked up a grape tomato and held it up to her sister’s lips. “Try this. It’s like any other tomato.”



    Kara had a knack for stopping fights before they could occur, and this time was no exception.



    “Hey Natty, this one looks like the leafy greens Littlefoot and his friends ate.” Kara held up the red leaf lettuce like it was a prize and showed it to Natty, who blinked at the curly red edges with interest. “Do you want to share with me and we’ll see if it makes you grow to be big and strong like the dinosaurs?”



    “There’s some on my plate you can have if you finish all of Kara’s first,” Andrea chimed in and separated out the special lettuce.



    For once Andrea wasn’t stirring trouble, and everyone at the table glanced in her direction to see if it was a trick.



    The usual hostility in Andrea’s eyes was overcast with a desperate longing not to be pushed aside by their youngest right after Sophia had snubbed her about the party. It must have taken Andrea a great deal of effort not to say anything about it and move on without causing a scene.



    Lena pitied her ex in that moment and offered Andrea the barest hint of a smile that encouraged her to keep striving to be better. She passed Natty over to her sire once she chomped the salad, and she was glad that Natty didn’t complain.



    It turned out it wasn’t Natty that Lena had to be worried about, because Andy took it upon herself to ask the questions the adults at the table couldn’t. “So did Alison officially ask you out or did she just bring you back a bracelet?”



    “She asked me out during lunch and gave me a card and chocolates that I shared with Ruby,” Sophia informed everyone with a pleased smile.



    Lillian casually alerted the waiter that she would like another drink while Andrea clenched her teeth so hard that even Lena could hear them grinding from across the table.



    “How romantic,” Andrea gritted under her breath and stabbed at a tomato on her plate.



    Natty tried to mimic the aggression and sent several olives flying.



    “Did she bring Taylor anything back from her trip?” Andy asked without meeting Sophia’s eyes. The casual tone she used was at odds with her tense posture, though she sold it with how bored she sounded.



    Lena knew her eldest was anything but, and everyone stopped eating to hear the irritated sigh Sophia released.



    “Alison got her a bunch of souvenirs, including a necklace that Taylor wears all of the time.” Sophia flicked through her friends’ social media pages and pointed out the gifts Taylor received.



    Lillian sneered at the images and grabbed her second Aperol Spritz. “When I was younger, I never liked getting too serious with alphas. Be a little rude and haughty. After pursuing Taylor, Alison should have to work twice as hard to win you over.”



    “Listen to your grandmother,” Andrea urged, reaching the edge of hysteria after glimpsing a photo of Alison bear-hugging her daughter. “She’s giving you very solid advice.”



    “Advice my own daughter never cared to take,” Lillian snidely muttered and flicked her lashes over Andrea without any sympathy.



    “The bracelet looks real and a lot nicer than the necklace,” Andy observed, keeping the peace through distraction and compliments. “Just don’t become more emotionally invested than she is and you won’t get hurt.”



    “I know that. I’m not stupid,” Sophia huffed, no doubt overwhelmed by everyone chiming in on her very first relationship. She fiddled with the bracelet like she sought comfort from it and blinked as if tears were welling in her eyes.



    “None of us think you are,” Kara insisted and looked to Lena as she carried on with good intentions to smooth things over. “We all remember our first loves and what an exciting and challenging time it was in our lives.”



    “Andy doesn’t. She’s never dated anyone.” Sophia tried to push the conversation towards her sister instead of remaining the focal point of the discussion.



    “By choice, not lack of opportunities,” Andy clarified before anyone decided to impart their own wisdom onto her about finding an omega. “If I’d dated someone at your age, I would have had to get our moms’ approval, and that isn’t a bad thing.”



    “She’s right,” Lena cut in and held off on taking Sophia’s hand in case her daughter thought she was trying to coddle her in some way. “We trust you and your judgment, but we don’t know Alison as well as you do and we want to make sure you’re going into this new stage of your life confidently with the knowledge that you’re in control of the situation.”



    Sophia pushed her fork through her food and smeared the sauce across the plate in her agitation. “Meaning what?”



    Kara fielded that question with the same even tone she used when handling any touchy subject. “Meaning it’s important to have boundaries with Alison and expectations that they aren’t crossed.



    Andrea coughed and dabbed at her lips with a napkin before fixing Sophia with a serious stare. “Say you want to hang out with Alison, but Alison wants to hang out with Taylor, too. Is that something you would accept?”



    Sophia reacted to the hypothetical situation as if it were happening and shoved her plate away in devastation. “No way! Why can’t Taylor hang out with her own friends?”



    “That right there? That’s a boundary,” Andrea explained with a wave of her knife and sliced through her quail to offer a piece to Natty. “You’ll have to make it clear to Alison that you’re not okay with her being friendly with Taylor if she wants to date you.”



    “If she doesn’t care, or does it anyway, then she doesn’t respect you,” Lena added with a hard glance at Andrea, who had the decency to keep her mouth shut.



    For their first real attempt at co-parenting, it was a success. Sophia appeared to be listening to their tips, and she had a plan for talking to Alison by the time their bill arrived.



    The next stop on their itinerary was the park by the lake, and Lena meandered between feeling excited and nervous about their pregnancy announcement.



    Kara took a proactive approach by speaking with Andrea to explain they were going to share the baby news with the kids. It turned out that being direct was better than Lena’s gut instinct to just keep it a secret until afterward in case her ex decided to ruin the whole afternoon for them.



    Andrea was unhappy that she couldn’t bow out of the trip to the lake on account of Lillian requiring a ride. At least she had the courtesy to suggest she stay in her Benz. It was the nicest thing she could have possibly done for them, though Lena wasn’t sure she trusted Andrea not to change her mind.



    Upon getting to their destination, Lena herded all of the kids towards the playground. Kara gathered a box from the trunk and set off towards some large boulders arranged along the water.



    Alex drove up in her classic vehicle and Ruby bolted from her car to hang out with Sophia.



    Sam stalked over to the playground with a complaint already on her lips. “They act like they aren’t together every day and night. We should have just skipped the tour of the school and met up with you guys for lunch.”



    Alex hung back to smile at the enthusiasm of the kids greeting each other.



    “You’re still feeling that empty nest, but guess what? Ruby missed you just as much. Why else would she care to show you around if not to soak up your attention?” Lena didn’t think twice about sharing her own observations, though she regretted it when Sam’s chin wobbled.



    Lena soothed her friend, and saved her from the embarrassment of crying by pulling her into a hug. “Hey, it’s okay. You’re both adjusting and it’ll take time.”



    They held onto one another for a long moment, and parted with watery smiles that they were quick to wipe away when Kara called out to gather everyone over.



    Andy was the first to reach Kara’s side, then Ruby and Sophia with Alex and Natty fast behind them.



    Lena avoided Sam’s curious eyes and ushered her along to find a dozen cupcakes that Kara brought and placed on one of the giant rocks.



    Kara clutched a large book in her hands that puzzled everyone, including Lena.



    “I know we’re all here for Parents Weekend and to spend time with the ones we love, and I just wanted to say I’m so grateful to be part of it,” Kara stated with a nervous lip bite that couldn’t quite conceal her smile. She shrugged off her clear anxiety and took a deep breath before flipping open the cover of the book to reveal it was a photo album.



    The first page started with a photo of the kids and Lena by the tree they had decorated for Christmas. Kara turned to the next to show the girls with Andrea celebrating New Year’s, and the adjacent side which had Lena, Lillian and Sam all toasting with sparklers in their hands.



    “I’ve spent the majority of my life working out what family means.” Kara’s voice wavered as she flipped through images of Alex and her friends meeting Lena and the girls. Eliza and Lillian laughing together at the claim party, and a few candid and hilarious shots of the girls making faces.



    “I know it looks different to everyone, but this is what it looks like to me.” Kara highlighted all the best moments together, from family dinners to date nights on the couch with kids. Messy shots of Natalia’s artwork covering the floor, and her paint-splattered face grinning up at the camera.



    “It’s all of you,” Kara said with so much emotion that everyone fell into a hush as she flipped through pictures of their vacation.



    Andrea held Natty on her hip with a genuine smile gracing her lips, while Bernardo stood proudly with Sophia and Andy. The album contained sunsets by the beach where the ocean reflected in Lillian’s sunglasses, and then a few selfies of Kara with each of the girls.



    “It’s choosing to be here for each other, and all the memories we make along the way,” Kara explained, showcasing another group photo from her birthday of everyone posing for the camera. Beside it was a snap of the girls with Ruby, grinning and covered in cake.



    “And all the memories we’re still going to make together as a family.” Kara hesitated for a fraction of a second, and turned to the last page where she slid in the ultrasound scan of their pup.



    Andy and Alex gasped, and Lillian flung her hand out to grab Lena’s as she teared up.



    “Are you being serious right now?” Andy demanded, and looked between her mother and Kara like she wasn’t sure if she should be happy or mad if it was a hoax.



    “They better be or I will never forgive them.” Lillian peered at Lena with remorse as she realized why Kara had been staring at her middle in Mexico.



    “We are,” Lena intoned and squeezed her mother’s hand to let her know she held no grudges.



    “Surprise!” Kara exclaimed, unable to breathe as she stared at Sophia, who had gone silent and stone faced. “The three of you are going to be big sisters again.”



    “No,” Sophia sniffled, and shattered all the hope Lena had that this would be a happy announcement.



    “No?” Kara raised her brows and tried not to show how that single word crushed her heart.



    “No,” Sophia reiterated forcefully and turned to the side, positioning herself as if to run off. “We’re not going to be big sisters. We’re going to be the best sisters. Right?”



    Sophia looked to Andy for affirmation, and narrowly avoided Natty’s feet as she wriggled out of Alex’s grip in excitement.



    “Natty, there’s a baby in Mama’s stomach.” Sophia grabbed her younger sibling by the hand and led her over to touch Lena’s bump.



    Natty patted the small swell and pressed her ear against it. “Hi baby. How did you get inside there?”



    “It swam like a mermaid.” Andy cringed at the accuracy of that lie and hurried to distract everyone from the uncomfortable details of expanding their family. “Why don’t we get some cupcakes?”



    The girls picked out iced cupcakes in all of their favorite flavors, and Lena slipped her arms around Kara. “Thank you for planning this and for letting me enjoy the surprise.”



    After three birth experiences, Lena came to expect a certain level of stress that would follow her through her later trimesters. The ease she felt this time was all due to Kara’s even-tempered nature. She trusted Kara to handle any circumstance that might arise with their family.



    “You deserve a weekend where you just get to be excited and you don’t have to do all of the preparation.” Kara reached for a chocolate cupcake and kept one arm looped around her. She peeled the paper off the cake and Lena accepted a bite of it.



    “I can’t believe you didn’t tell me first,” Sam lamented over dramatically and pulled her huge sunglasses off so everyone would see her puffy eyes. “I’m offended, but I guess it’s fair play for all of the secrets I’ve kept from you over the years.”



    Lena knocked her elbow into her best friend and handed her a strawberry cupcake. “Sam was the actually the first to find out. She happened to be at our house after I took a pregnancy test.”



    “I won’t stoop so low as to ask how long you’ve known, because I can take comfort that I’m not the last oneto find out.” Lillian’s teasing remark didn’t bring any laughter from Lena and she paused with a cupcake at her lips to blink in the direction of Andrea’s Benz.



    “Tell me she didn’t–” Lillian sputtered in offense and gaped at Lena like she had betrayed her personally. “Before me?”



    Lena froze with panicked eyes and relaxed when Kara stepped in front of her to smooth over any hurt feelings Lillian might have. “That was my slip up, and absolutely not how we planned for Andrea finding out. It doesn’t change how special the news is and how important it was for us to announce it when you were here.”



    “Speak of the devil,” Sam murmured under her breath as Andrea stepped out of her vehicle and then appeared lost as to what to do next. She stood awkwardly by her Benz and stared off to the playground where Natty would play after eating her cupcake.



    Nobody seemed sure of what to do or how uncomfortable it could be for Andrea to be there after announcing the pregnancy.



    Kara excused herself to hug Alex, and then detoured by the box of cupcakes to lift one of each flavor. Lena didn’t find it odd until she strode over to Andrea and offered her both.



    The tension between them could be felt a hundred yards away, and everyone fell silent to watch. It was nothing short of a miracle that Kara didn’t wind up wearing one of the cupcakes when Andrea painstakingly chose the strawberry shortcake one without so much as a thank you.



    It was an olive branch her ex-wife didn’t deserve, and Lena was surprised by the relief it gave her when Andrea accepted it without malice.



    Kara motioned to the group, who all instinctively tried to act natural and resumed chatting so it wasn’t obvious how invested they were in the potential drama that might take place between them.



    Andrea made her way over with slow, careful steps like she presumed she would be rejected by everyone. Kara did her the mercy of returning to Lena’s side to eat her own treat without forcing her to interact.



    Andy wasn’t nearly as tactful as she squinted up at her sire with a critical furrow of her brows. “Have you been crying?”



    Andrea gave an irritable sniff and ripped the paper casing off her cupcake while avoiding her oldest daughter’s eyes. “No, your grandmother’s perfume is just caustic and has ruined the interior of my car.”



    Lillian gave a bitter laugh and rounded on Andrea with a tight-lipped expression. “You should be thanking me for gracing your nostrils with something other than that disgusting air freshener.”



    “It’s cedar combined with a collection of pheromones to stimulate the mind,” Andrea scoffed like she thought Lillian was too old to appreciate the ingenuity of such a product. “It’s new on the market and costs more than the outfit you're wearing.”



    “It’s pretentious and smells like mothballs.” Lillian’s scathing remark simultaneously caused Andy to choke on her cupcake and laugh.



    Lena refused to intervene because it was cheap entertainment to see her mother swap harmless barbs with her ex, and everyone else looked just as amused.



    Ruby and Sophia ran off to the rocks for privacy and animatedly discussed Sophia’s upcoming party.



    Andy took Natty over to the swings and roped Alex into joining her by saying it would be great practice if she was wanting to have kids with Sam.



    The lack of terror in Alex’s eyes set off Sam’s radar, and Lena pulled her friend aside before she had a panic attack about the future of her relationship.



    “Look it’s not that I’m opposed to having more kids —I’ve just been doing a lot of thinking," Sam huffed.



    Lena worried that her best friend was going to reveal that she didn’t want to be with Alex or that there was some other problem in their relationship.



    Sam’s eyes darted between Ruby and Alex like she was trying to piece together a puzzle that didn’t make sense. “What if - what if we already have one?”



    Lena assumed her friend was experiencing paranoia related to a potential pup and how Sam planned to explain it to her daughter. She grasped her friend’s hand in excitement and leaned in to whisper, “Wait, you think you’re also expecting?”



    Sam recoiled so fast that she would have fallen if Lena hadn’t held onto her arm.



    “Fuck no,” Sam hissed and made an effort to lower her voice in case someone over heard them. “I have my uterus locked down with the best birth control money can buy.”



    Lena blinked in confusion for all of two seconds and then her mind went into overdrive and she stared pointedly at Sam, who flinched under the scrutiny. “Then I don’t understand what you mean. Ruby’s sire was that asshole who left. That’s what you told me.”



    “That’s what I believed, but what if I was wrong?” Sam asked and anxiously turned to observe Alex and how she tilted her head to listen to Andy. Ruby did the same thing while talking to Sophia and Sam reacted by covering her mouth in panic. “What if I was already pregnant when I hooked up with that idiot, and I just naturally assumed?”



    Lena sagged under the weight of those questions and tried not to let her emotions get in the way of her logic.



    If this was true, and Alex turned out to be Ruby’s sire, the news would either make or break their relationship. There was no telling how either of them might respond if Sam’s speculations were real, and if it would ruin the family dynamic they had only just settled into over the past month.



    “Sam–”



    “I know. I know, okay?” Sam frantically blurted and brushed her hair back when the wind blew it into her face. “That would be screwed up, but Lena, I keep seeing similarities between them and now I’m questioning everything. Like is
    this just a wild fantasy my mind is creating because I want someone like Alex in Ruby’s life or are they actually related? What the hell should I do?”



    “Tell her, like immediately,” Lena commanded in a much shriller and bossier tone that she ever used with Sam. “Alex is practically my sister-in-law and you’re my family. I’m sure it’s frightening, but Alex is great with kids. Just look at her over there with Natty. She’s pretending to launch her in a rocket ship.”



    Sam observed the squealing laughter on the playground and Alex’s beaming smile. “Fuck. I know I should just do it, but you have no idea how stubborn Alex can be. She’s going to be pissed off that I didn’t think of this sooner and contact her.”



    “Oh no, Alex is reasonable,” Lena advocated out of a desperation to keep her family intact. “She’s going to understand. Kara wouldn’t hold it against you, and Alex is going to be so happy—”



    Sam pressed her fingers into her forehead and let out a soft laugh. “Maybe with Ruby, but not with me. We had a fight once because I forgot to tell her our plant died.”



    Lena wasn’t in the habit of dismissing Sam’s fears, but she couldn’t fathom why one fight over a plant was reason enough to stay silent about something so serious. “That was what, fourteen years ago? Alex was probably just stressed out. You know how that is.”



    “You’re right. I do know,” Sam insisted with a level of panic that made her a little aggressive. “The Danvers’ sisters are practically unicorns, but nobody is perfect all of the time, Lena, and neither are they.”



    The ominous warning didn’t sit right with Lena but she chalked it up to worry on Sam’s part as her friend walked off to grab a bottle of water.



    She knew better than to push the subject right then, and wandered over to Kara just in time to catch her trying to engage Andrea in conversation.



    “I’m not about to congratulate you if that’s what you want,” Andrea hissed at Kara and stared straight ahead to where Natty laughed on the swing.



    Kara circumvented the animosity by refusing to get her ego involved. She leaned on the fence like she was completely at ease in the face of hostility and shrugged. “I’d rather talk about Sophia’s party. I know she asked for my help, but I’d like to have yours in organizing it so that it’s truly special for her.”



    Lena didn’t want to intrude because her presence might set off Andrea and derail all of the effort Kara was putting into bringing their family together.



    She walked off before either of them caught wind of her pheromones and almost bumped into Sophia and Ruby.



    “Mom, Alison just texted that she’s in town with her sire. Can I invite her to go bowling with us?” Sophia asked so fast that she sounded breathless with excitement. “I want to tell her in person about my party and that I don’t want Taylor to come.”



    Lena would have preferred to keep it a family evening, but the news about her pregnancy had gone so well that she didn’t see the harm in caving to Sophia’s request.



    “Sure, you can invite Alison, and it will give us the chance to talk to her sire.”



    Their plans for the evening involved splitting into two teams for a friendly competition at the local bowling alley. Lena liked the place because it served alcohol for adults. She couldn’t partake this time, but her first stop after picking up shoes was to the concession stand.



    Her cravings were starting to kick in, and now that everyone knew her secret, she took guilt-free enjoyment in an order of nachos. After she finished, she dipped a large pretzel into the leftover cheese sauce. She made eye contact with Kara and hurried to wipe her lips with a napkin.



    “Oh, mmm, you have to try this while we’re here.” Lena glanced around towards the lanes where their children were picking out bowling balls.



    Kara kissed a taste of the food right from Lena’s lips without making any comments about her appearance. “That’s really good. Give me another taste.”



    Lena smirked and slipped her hand onto the back of Kara’s belt. She locked her lips with Kara’s and laughed into the kiss. Few times in her life had been so carefree, and Kara went out of her way to be affectionate.



    “So, I was thinking about splitting us up.” Kara motioned back at the teams made up of their family members. “We’re probably too powerful together.”



    “No, we’re not,” Lena chuckled and swirled her pretzel through the remaining cheese. She discarded her trash and decided to spin the balls in the nearest rack to select one. “I’m terrible at bowling. One time I threw my ball into another lane and earned someone else points.”



    Kara inspected the balls, picked one out for her and helped to slide it onto Lena’s fingers. She stood behind Lena and guided her by the elbow and wrist. “Try this technique. Bend your knees a little, and when you release, think about the best orgasm you’ve ever had.”



    Lena smiled at her mate, grateful for the instructions and their little moments together. “You’re trying to seduce me at family bowling. Why is it that you can make every outing infinitely better?”



    “It’s just my superpower.” Kara shrugged by tucking her chin and lifting her hands up. “I want you to have fun. This is a special family moment and nothing can mess with it. Not Andrea, not my cousin. I’m at peace with everyone tonight.”



    Lena slipped her fingers through Kara’s and they headed for the lanes to play their first round.



    The kids were munching on snacks and picking team names, and Lena became distracted with a joyful daydream of the baby that would join them in the future.



    “Alison!” Sophia shouted, catapulting herself from the nearest seat to greet her friend.



    Lena turned around to scrutinize the sporty-looking alpha teen who stood at least an entire head taller than Sophia.



    Alison smelled of an alpha-specific perfume and dressed in clean-cut clothes — and Lena liked that the girl seemed nervous.



    Alison gave a small wave and hung back under Andrea’s intimidating stare. “It’s nice to meet everyone in Sophia’s big family.”



    Kara placed her arms across her chest, casually displaying her guns for all to see, but not in a way that was completelyunfriendly. She glanced towards Andrea, who nodded to her and continued to look miserable as Sophia dragged Alison off to pick out a ball.



    Lena smirked at her mate’s odd way of bonding with her ex in their mutual dislike of someone that could break their daughter’s heart. “The two of you can tone it down a bit. You’re going to scare the poor kid.”



    She turned around to grab her bag and came face-to-face with someone she hadn’t seen in a long time. Not since her boarding school days, or maybe college.



    Alison’s sire was an alpha she knew intimately, who chased her during the in-betweens of her relationship with Andrea – and who had once called her the one that got away.



    “Lucy,” Lena warbled, her lips continuing to move for no reason around another attempt to voice her name.



    “Lena.” Lucy grinned at her and came in for a hug like the passage of time changed nothing between them. “I’ve been meaning to reach out ever since Alison told me there’s a Rojas in her class. I’m not surprised they’ve become good friends over the years. We were always so close.”



    “We were,” Lena agreed, sounding much softer than was acceptable for meeting up with someone who was just an old friend.



    “Too close,” Andrea muttered far too loudly to ignore and postured in the background for a new reason.



    Lena nibbled her lip and stepped back to take Kara’s hand and make introductions. “Lucy, this is my—"



    “Wife?” Lucy asked, in part as a clear jab at Andrea. She must have learned some information about Lena’s life from Alison, except for the detail that she had never remarried.



    “No, umm, we’re mates – but we’re not married yet.” Lena snuck a fast glance over at Kara’s stoic face.



    Lucy smiled so wide her lipstick could have rubbed against her teeth.



    Kara stuck out her hand to shake Lucy’s, even as she behaved more standoffishly than she ever had in the past.



    “I’m Kara.”

    Chapter 32

    Chapter Notes

    Running into former classmates from boarding school was never a positive experience for Lena. Since enrolling her two oldest children at her alma mater, she bumped into a lot of people she knew — not just at special events for parents, but also during drop-offs and pick-ups in between sessions. All of those interactions tended to be strained or awkward. In an environment like DC Prep where everyone was successful in their own right, being divorced with three kids was seen as a personal failure — something that she should have been able to control. Lena heaped enough blame onto herself for making terrible decisions when she was young and foolishly in love. She didn’t need anyone else silently adding onto it.

    Lena was no longer ashamed of her divorced status, and she certainly didn’t regret being with Andrea because it gave her three incredible children—however, she still preferred to avoid anyone from that stage of her life.


    Lucy behaved much differently than her other old classmates. She didn’t look at Lena with pity or judgment, and her familiarity took the pressure off when it came to Sophia. If any issues arose between their kids, Lena knew she could have a candid discussion with Lucy and brainstorm ways of dealing with all of the pre-teen drama together.


    The only downside was that Lena couldn’t exactly pull Kara aside and explain her full history with Lucy in a way that would be sufficient in a brief chat. She owed Kara more than two minutes of her time, and with so many kids to look after, they couldn’t leave them unattended.


    It was no wonder that Kara postured the entire time that Lucy spent sorting through the bowling balls and buying refreshments.


    Lena could only imagine what her mate was thinking, and she did her best to appear laid back so the kids wouldn’t realize the tension between them.


    She caught Kara’s eye with a pinched smile and hurried towards her while everyone else was busy.


    The best she could do was give Kara a very condensed version of her past with Lucy and hope that it would suffice until they got to their hotel later.


    Lena fussed with the front of Kara’s shirt just for the sake of touching her. “I’m sorry this is awkward. If I’d known Lucy was Alison’s sire, I wouldn’t have agreed for them to join us tonight when we were celebrating our good news. Lucy and I never technically dated, but we did blur the lines of our friendship a few times during high school and college. Obviously she and Andrea hated each other. We drifted apart naturally once our lives started. It’s almost a stroke of luck to see her again.”


    Lena knew she said the wrong thing when Kara’s pheromones took on a defensive quality. Confusion entered Kara’s eyes and she took a step back to blink down at Lena.


    “Luck?” Kara arched her brows and crossed her arms to posture fully. The sharp cut of her jaw looked like she clenched her teeth and she cast a wary glance towards Lucy. “That’s an interesting way to describe seeing your not-quite-ex.”


    “It was a long time ago.” Lena softened her voice and brought Kara’s focus back onto herself by brushing her fingertips along the solid length of her forearm. “Isn’t it at least a little lucky that we aren’t completely navigating through Sophia’s first dating experiences with a parent we don’t know?”


    Kara snapped out of her funk at the realization that their get-together was only happening because of their middle child. She gazed over at the teens like she had forgotten they were there and smiled at the way they crowded around a phone to watch stupid videos.


    “I guess it’s better than flying totally blind,” Kara conceded and shook out her arms to slip one loosely around Lena’s hip.


    The intimacy calmed their frayed nerves, and Kara breathed deeper to catch the scent of her.


    Lena was on the cusp of believing that their afternoon would work out just fine when her mother decided to insert herself in the discussion.


    Lillian approached with a gleam in her eye and paused right in front of Lena so she couldn’t escape. “Lena, isn’t that the alpha who gave you the giant love bite that went against all school regulations—”


    Lena burned at those little reminders and put a hand on her mother’s arm to direct her out of the way. “Mother, why can’t you be more forgetful of the things I did to defy you?”


    “It’s my only means of revenge after all of these years, and trust me Ideserve revenge given the amount of stress you caused me.” Lillian curled her lips into a pleased smile and peered towards the refreshments to observe Lucy paying for an extra-large soda.


    Kara’s relaxed attitude vanished along with the arm around Lena’s waist. She exhaled sharply and tilted her head as she folded her arms a little higher up. “So now I have two alphas I need to watch around my family instead of just one.”


    Andrea scoffed at her assumptions like she hadn’t been the bane of their relationship. “Please. You don’t have to worry about little old me. Lucy is far more trouble.”


    “I didn’t mean you.” Kara dropped out of her brooding posture again and glanced around at the gathering of kids. “I meant Alison.”


    Before any new frictions could arise between them, Kara walked off to monitor the teens a little more closely.


    Lucy wandered over with an armful of refreshments and no idea that she was the subject of their discussion. She sipped her soda and sized Kara up as her primary competitor at bowling. “So, whose team am I on?”


    “Mine,” Lillian interjected with a fast up-and-down of Lucy’s casual pantsuit. “You’ll be with me, Sam and Alex. We’ll go up against Kara, Andrea, Natty and Lena.”


    They would have two games going at once with Andy, Sophia, Alison and Ruby facing off against Kara, Alex, Lillian and Sam. That way everyone would get the chance to participate and the teens would feel like they had real competition.


    Natty had fallen asleep on one of the cushioned seats with her arms wrapped around a squishmallow and a dusting of churro sugar on her face. Someone would have to wake her before the first round.


    “I don’t mean to be so stereotypically alpha, but I play to win,” Lucy announced, looking over at her opponents and then letting her eyes wander to Lena like she was the trophy and not an opposing teammate. “I can go pretty hard.”


    Lena didn’t perceive the remark as anything sexual, but Kara and Andrea both reacted as if Lucy had made a statement about some graphic act she wanted to perform.


    Kara puffed up like an over-inflated balloon and Andrea decided to spread the reach of her protective stink.


    Sam appeared at just the right time to walk into a wall of their pheromones. “Hey, what did I miss?”


    “A lot,” Lena emphasized through gritted teeth and grabbed her best friend by the wrist to reel her in. “Where were you?”


    Given the jean jacket Sam wore, a reasonable guess was outside - too far from the action to make sense of who Lucy was and why Kara peacocked as she grabbed her ball.


    “I was having a quick chat with Alex in the car.” Sam motioned with her eyes to where her girlfriend lingered at the entrance of the bowling alley, shell-shocked and much slower to approach the group.


    Alex wandered towards Ruby first, who came up to side-hug her and missed all of her stunned and afflicted facial expressions.


    “How did she take it?” Lena asked under her breath in case anyone overheard what they were talking about. She could feel the atmospheric shift between Alex and Sam and instinctively grabbed for her best friend’s hand to offer comfort.


    “Like I’d handed her a grenade and ran off with the pin.” Sam worried her lip and stared at her girlfriend until tears welled in her eyes. She blew out a heavy breath and fussed with her hair, finger-combing it to hide the rapid way she blinked back her own emotion before the kids saw it. “I expected her to get hot tempered, maybe yell or demand answers, but it was like everything drained out of her and she just sat there and said nothing.”


    “She has a lot to process, though I will say actions speak louder than words.” Lena nudged Sam into glancing over to where Alex was helping Ruby pick out a bowling ball. In the middle of their conversation, Alex’s eyes kept landing on Sam. “You don’t look at someone like that unless it’s love. Just give her time to come to terms with the possibility that you two already share a child.


    “Speaking of looking, who the hell is that and why can’t she take her eyes off you?” Sam asked the moment she finally noticed Lucy and how Kara strutted around her like she was at a photoshoot and not a bowling alley.


    Lena tucked her chin to her chest and laughed to avoid obvious Sam’s wariness and Lucy’s smile. It wasn’t that she found the situation funny so much as conflicting and awkward. “That’s Lucy, Alison’s sire. We have a little shared history between us.”


    It would have been much easier to recount events without Andrea hovering in the background and jumping in to dispute the facts.


    “A little history? You snuck around with her all of the time at boarding school, and I know that you hooked up at least twice when we were in college.”


    Some of Sam’s pep returned from finding that out and realizing just how much it rattled Andrea.


    “Wait, Lucy is that alpha you told me about years ago?” Sam asked in a quiet but eager voice. “The one who almostprevented you from making the worst mistake of your life with Andrea?”


    With the three of them gathered off to the side, Sam’s question only torpedoed Andrea’s mood.


    Andrea firmed her lips together and stared at Lena—not with her usual rage, but in solemn disappointment.


    Lena threw out her hand to halt Andrea from storming off. “Okay, maybe our relationship wasn’t the best, but we did get three great kids out of it. Let’s just try not to live in the past tonight. The past is meaningless.”


    In her effort to soothe her ex, Lena had missed Alex’s fast approach from behind their little group along and the clearly upset look on her face.


    “Are you all talking about what we just discussed?” Alex interrupted, concluding that they were all huddled because Sam had mentioned their chat about Ruby. “Am I the last person to know?”


    “What? No!” Sam overreacted, her voice reaching a high note and volume that could only be achieved by guilt. “This has nothing to do with us.”


    “I don’t know how much I trust that,” Alex countered with a deceptive softness that went against the stern frown on her face. “You knew there was a chance Ruby was mine, and you just sat on that information for thirteen years. How could you do that to me? I missed her entire childhood.”


    The shift in drama sucked Andrea in and she turned to Alex in obvious shock. “You’re Ruby’s sire?” She asked, a scoff forming on her lips as she turned to eye Sam with obvious judgment.


    “We don’t know that yet,” Sam explained with a fraught glance towards the kids, who were waiting for them to come over. “Please keep your voice down. This is hard enough without you broadcasting it to everyone.”


    “Maybe you should have told her somewhere privately and sooner instead of waiting for when we’re out with our kids,” Andrea fired back and in a twisted show of solidarity she sidled up to Alex to glare at Sam.


    Lena could sense the awful pleasure that Andrea derived from the terrible situation because for once she wasn’t the one getting called out for being a bad parent. She stared at her ex and threatened her through her pheromones to back off. “Andrea–”


    “No, she’s got a point,” Alex uttered, shocking even Andrea with her cold and quiet tone that demanded answers. “Why do this here and now when we’ve had weeks alone together? Of all the times to tell me, why in front of everyone?”


    “It wasn’t intentional, Alex. It’s just when I saw the two of you together again…” Sam grimaced at their predicament and folded her arms across herself to appear stronger in the face of Alex’s wrath. “I don’t know if it’s from the months you’ve been around one another, or if it’s wishful thinking on my part, but there are similarities between you. I couldn’t just unsee it, okay? I’m sorry.”


    “Sorry doesn’t rewind time, does it? We’re never getting those years back,” Alex hissed, the hurt in her tone cracking along with her composure. She looked furious and the distinct scent of betrayal clung to her pores.


    “I might have fucked up here by not getting a test, but you had already left, Alex.” Sam swung her arm to gesture wildly about the distance between them at that point. “You were deployed half the world away, so what difference would it have made? You weren’t coming back for years anyway. That's why we broke up!”


    Alex drew herself up to posture and acted every bit like the biological alpha she was while getting in Sam’s face. “If I had known you were carrying my pup, I would have been there!”


    “How?” Sam snapped, her anger pinching her brows together as she went head to head with her girlfriend. “You can’t just leave the military when you feel like it. They would arrest you for going AWOL.”


    The stark reminder took the wind out of Alex and she shrank a couple of inches as she deflated in misery. Silence hung between them, heavy and atmospheric.


    “Come on, mom!” Sophia yelled and waved her arms in the air to get their attention. “We’re all waiting to start!”


    “Switch teams with me,” Sam pleaded and took hold of Lena’s arm so she couldn’t walk off immediately. “I can’t be near Alex right now or the kids will know something is wrong.”


    Sam took it for granted that Lena would agree and hurried off to where Kara was rousing Natty with a pink ball that fit her little fingers.


    Lena didn’t realize the error she had made until Kara’s wounded eyes tracked her walking towards the other lane.


    Alex and Lillian stood uncomfortably beside Lucy, who looked like she had already won.


    Kara watched her for a couple of seconds before entering the names for each team onto the sign boards. She kept her brows in a serious crinkle, her body language devoid of the playful spirit she often brought to games like bowling.


    Lena frowned at her team and grabbed a ball that she could barely lift from the rack. “I hope you’re all prepared to lose gracefully with me on your side.”


    She noticed that she was slated to go first and considered putting up the bumpers. Just as she eyed a nearby ball-ramp meant for children, Lucy wandered up beside her and took hold of her wrist.


    “You’re not bad at bowling,” Lucy chided, helping out by sliding Lena’s fingers loose of the ball. “This is just too big for you. Maybe Andrea can pitch in and grab you something smaller.”


    The insinuation and crack at Andrea’s size would have been hilarious if not for the brewing jealousies in the air. Lena was about to take a step back when Kara sauntered over with another ball—not much smaller than the one Lena picked out, but far lighter.


    “This one should be just right for you.” Kara held it out for Lena to slip her fingers into the holes.


    They shared intense eye contact, and Lena tried to convey everything she felt in the soft caress of her fingers over Kara’s as she accepted the ball. “Thank you. You always know exactly what I need.”


    She wished she could have explained to her mate that she might be Ruby’s aunt, but this wasn’t the time or place for that conversation when Lucy was nearby. All she could do was point Kara in the right direction to seek answers.


    “Sam decided she wanted to be on your team instead. I couldn’t say no.”


    The partial truth was enough to lessen some of the tension in Kara’s shoulders and restore her smile. It was a fleeting thing that brightened her eyes more than her face, but Lena basked in it until the moment was ruined by her mother.


    “Well, are we bowling or not?” Lillian huffed and set her ball down to shake out her wrist and fingers like they ached already. “Some of us aren’t capable of handling balls the way we once did when we were younger.”


    Andy snorted two lanes down and Lena was mortified to hear her eldest mutter, “That’s what she said.”


    “Well on that note, may the best team win.” Kara’s friendly banter set the games in motion, and she hurried over to Natty, who was taking her first throw with Andrea.


    The little one used the ball-ramp, and she let out a cheer before any of the pins even toppled over.


    Andy earned her team eight points with her first throw, and Lena watched as her own ball shot down the polished wood and landed straight in the gutter.


    Laughter erupted from the kids until Lucy shocked them into silence by hitting a strike on her first try. Her self-assured swagger and posturing distracted Kara, who nearly lined up a shot on the kids’ lane instead.


    “Keep your head in the game. We have to win this,” Andrea coached and pointed to the pins waiting to be knocked over.


    “We can’t beat our kids,” Kara protested, though the sound of Lucy earning another strike seemed to change her mind. She lined up her shot with focus on her face, which went right out the window when Lucy intoned, “Come on Lena, I know your wrist action is better than that.”


    The flirty jeering snapped Kara out of her play and she released the ball far too soon and sent it bouncing down the lane.


    Andrea handed her another ball and shoved her back towards the adults’ lane with the kind of intensity she usually reserved for the kids. “Block it all out. Nobody here has biceps as big as you, so use them to knock those pins over.”


    The odd pep talk worked because Kara flexed and flung the ball so forcefully she not only earned a strike, she snapped the head off one of the pins.


    “Whoa, your step-sire is a beast,” Alison uttered in awe and stared at Kara with wide, intimidated eyes.


    “I know, right?” Sophia plucked up a ball and prepared herself to take a shot with competitive accuracy. “I’m sure you’re going to be just as strong some day.”


    “You think so?” Alison stood taller beside Sophia with all the tentative signs of learning to posture in order to impress a mate. It would have been sweet if Alison hadn’t then decided to help Sophia line-up her second shot by placing her hands on her hips.


    The mild peacocking caught all the adults' attention, and unfortunately Andy’s as well.


    “Nope, but you certainly compensate for it by posturing,” Andy stated matter of fact and grabbed her ball to flex beside Alison. The intimidation tactic worked on the younger alpha and Alison gulped and dropped her hands before Andy removed them for her.


    Andrea, Kara, and Alex looked pleased with the way Andy stepped in to keep the kids a respectful distance from each other, but it mortified Lena to see her eldest pulling rank.


    “Andy,” Lena hissed in a tone that made it clear she should stop.


    “She’s just joking and she’s sorry,” Ruby assured her friends and grabbed Andy by the arm to lead her over to the snacks.


    Observing the dynamics in the teen group wasn’t too different from observing the dynamics in the adult group.


    One of the bowling alley employees had to retrieve the pin Kara wrecked. Andy asked to keep it for the bragging rights, and in the meantime, Alex took her shot with a striking power that could only be fueled by anger.


    Lucy went to high-five her, and Alex reciprocated it, even though she threw Lena a baffled look. She mouthed “Who is this?” and pulled a smile on her face whenever Lucy happened to glance her way.


    “I forgot to make introductions. Alex, this is Lucy, Alison’s sire.” Lena sucked in a breath which she held in her nostrils for too long before exhaling. “We also went to boarding school together. Lucy, this is Alex, Kara’s older sister and Sam’s girlfriend.”


    In short order, Alex worked out that her sister’s tension related back to Lucy’s presence. Her lips formed an “oh” and she put out her hand in greeting. “Great to meet you.”


    “It’s nice getting to know everyone in Lena’s new circle.” Lucy smiled and grabbed the seat next to Lena with a fond glance over her every feature.


    It was common courtesy to smile in return, though Lena regretted it when Lucy’s pheromones encroached on her space. She didn’t mean to blush at the clear interest she was being shown, and it stunned her that Lucy was at ease with letting it be known.


    “Things have changed over the years,” Lillian intoned with a shrewd glance at Lucy once she detected her flirtatious musk. “I’ve never seen my daughter so happy and I’m thankful we’re all here as a family.”


    “As am I,” Lena insisted, loud enough for Kara and Andrea to overhear. She shifted to meet her mate’s gaze but the move brought her closer to Lucy, who seemed to appreciate the intimacy of staring into her eyes.


    “With the way things are going, I might be part of the family some day.” Lucy’s playful lilt pinned Lena to the spot until she peered across at their daughters.


    Sophia brushed a few crumbs off of Alison’s sports top and they both giggled as they held hands and shared the same churro. Andy was too busy bowling to interrupt their moment, though the minute she knocked over several pins, Sophia took her hand back and Alison raced her to their seats.


    Lena’s optimism for things working out for Sophia was dampened by her own experiences, and she tipped her head to the side to touch the claims on her throat. “First loves rarely stick. We can just hope that they’ll remain good friends.”


    “Like we were until after college.” Lucy lowered her eyes to the double-claim on Lena’s throat, oblivious to the effect that her attentions were having on everyone else.


    Kara stopped bowling altogether to watch their conversation and Lena decided that she needed to shut Lucy down in a gentle manner.


    “We weren’t first loves. We weren’t even girlfriends.” Lena raised her chin as she gave that reminder and squinted at Lucy in an attempt to figure out what the hell she was doing being so forward in front of everyone.


    “We could have been if I’d just been a little faster with sharing my feelings.” Lucy bumped Lena with a playful elbow and then lifted her drink to chew at the straw instead of her lower lip. It was clear where her mind went with the way her gaze lingered on Lena’s mouth.


    “That feels like forever ago, but I firmly believe that everything worked out the way it was meant to work out.” Lena redirected Lucy’s attention to everyone else around them with a simple gesture to the kids who were playing and the adults that were all very tense and obviously eavesdropping. “We both have wonderful children. I have a mate that I absolutely adore and who adores me just the same. I’m sure you’ll find that with someone if you haven’t already.”


    The distancing technique pulled Lucy out of her tunnel vision and she closed her eyes with a self-deprecating groan. “I’ve been a bit of an ass, haven’t I?”


    Andrea wasn’t at all subtle in the background with how she nodded along to Lucy’s self-assessment. Lena hardly paid attention to that asinine behavior when Kara was actively trying to ignore their conversation by helping Natty roll the ball without the ramp.


    Lena mindlessly rubbed her hand over her middle, and the private and loving pheromones of her claim drifted over to Kara. “You’ve certainly made some waves with how you’ve been acting.”


    Lucy had the good grace to scoot herself back several inches so she wasn’t sitting so close to Lena. She raised her hands apologetically and leaned into the seat with a sigh. “Seeing you again just brought back so many memories and I got swept up in them. I’m sorry about that, Lena. You’ve barely aged and here I am acting as young as you look.”
