    That shook Kara out of her meek state, and her alpha unfurled as she sat forward to pin Cat with an intense stare. “This is off the record, right? I’m not consenting to anything I say being used in a story just so we’re clear. I’m here out of courtesy, not for a pay check.”


    Lena slid her hand onto Kara’s thigh out of pride as she used her private, claim pheromones to relax her mate. She took control of the situation when Kara sat back to allow her the lead, and met Cat’s gaze head on. “My ex-wife used Siobhan to pose as an investor to waste Kara’s time and interfere in our relationship. She then entered a relationship with Nia to keep tabs on us. We found all of this out at the photo-shoot, and Kara quite rightfully knocked Andrea on her ass for all of the trouble, stress and heartache she had caused.”


    She made it a point to place her free hand on her abdomen to signal she was pregnant, and then swept the hair away from her neck to show off the claims there. It wasn’t exactly subtle, but it made it clear why Kara might have reacted so harshly given the circumstances.


    Cat sucked on her teeth and folded her hands in her lap as she deliberated on what to say in light of the new information presented. She flicked her lashes towards Kara and then back to Lena like she was assessing their relationship. “Do you know what a story like this could do? It could ruin Andrea Rojas in a matter of hours. You could be on every talk show across the nation with this kind of scandal. So why aren’t you?”


    “Because there are more important things in life than revenge and money.” Kara spat, righteous in her anger but not at all overbearing as she squared her jaw. She clasped Lena’s hand in solidarity and released a protective musk that Cat shooed away with her notebook. “Lena’s kids are my kids, and I’m not going to drag their sire across social media for five minutes of fame. This affects their lives, and I won’t jeopardize their relationship with Andrea for anything, even my own peace of mind.”


    Cat removed her glasses and pressed the tip of the frame to her lips for a moment. “Spoken like someone who hasn’t thought of the bigger picture. Do you think Andrea Rojas would be as lenient with you if the situation was reversed? If you went public with this story, you would have no shortage of people interested in your little pool projects.”


    “I don’t care what Andrea would do in my shoes. I’m still not interested,” Kara reinforced through gritted teeth.


    Anyone would sweat under that kind of pressure. Most would bend or break when faced with the potential of achieving their dreams by any means necessary, but not Kara. She stayed firm, sat tall and didn’t waver for a single second.


    Lena wanted to commend Kara on the strength of her backbone and express how wildly attractive she found her, though it was neither the time nor place for those antics. She had to content herself with gliding her palm over Kara’s thigh to get her message across – subtle and slow and a slight bit feral with the way she dug her nails into the fabric of Kara’s pants, like she couldn’t wait to tear them off.


    Kara didn’t react physically as far as Lena could tell, but her pheromones sure did. They coiled around Lena like an invisible force to tantalize her omega, holding her in a state of semi-arousal.


    “So you’re not out for revenge or to make a quick buck, and you have no intention to go public for any reason. Do you know what that makes you?” Cat raised her chin more than her brows and folded her arms across her chest as she waited for an answer.


    “A good person?” Kara’s confusion came out as a question and she side-eyed Lena to see if she agreed with her assessment.


    “Boring,” Cat drawled in exasperation and flung her hands up in a mockery of a celebration. “Congratulations, Kara, you’re as average as they come. Is it any wonder that Andrea strung you along with Siobhan for months and dated your close friend when this is how you act?”


    “Excuse me?” One moment Kara was sitting next to Lena, and the next she was on her feet like she might just walk out.


    Lena was livid on Kara’s behalf, and she drew Cat a scathing look as she stood up with every intention of getting them the hell out of the office. She owed Kara an apology for persuading her to show up, but she had always known Cat to be an upstanding omega if not a bit eccentric.


    “You’re young and idealistic, and you think you’re rising above it all but guess what? You’re not.” Cat’s matter of fact tone cut through the fast-forming tension and served to agitate Kara further. She rolled her eyes at the posturing and remained seated as she pointed her pen at Kara and ignored Lena entirely. “You’ll say you’re trying to be noble for the children, but all you’re really doing is showing the world you’re a doormat. Do you know what happens to the rich and powerful when nobody holds them accountable? Nothing. Where’s your fire?”


    “It was in my fist when I slammed it into Andrea’s face,” Kara admitted, her hands balled by her sides. She contorted her face in frustration at losing her composure and huffed out a heavy breath as she tried to let go of her anger.


    “Look, I get it, okay?” Kara swept her hand through the air to point to the giant TV screens behind Cat and paced in front of the couch like she was trying to make a case for herself. “Every channel could report your story and people would snap up your magazine, but that doesn’t help me, and it won’t help Andrea.”


    Kara’s outburst brought genuine surprise to Cat’s features, and she blinked twice before reclining in her seat to stare at the alpha in bewilderment. “You want to help the billionaire that’s systematically tormented you for months on end? Are you being blackmailed or paid off?”


    “None of those things!” Kara insisted with a gobsmacked expression. She had lost her anxiety in the fast back-and-forth but she still grimaced under the heavy glare of Cat’s sharp eyes. “This is worse than I imagined it would be, but with all due respect, Miss Grant, you’re wrong about me not seeing the bigger picture. Maybe Andrea doesn’t deserve my silence for what she did, but she’s going to get it anyway because I believe she can be a better person. If not for herself, then for the kids, and she won’t achieve that if you publish what happened. Please, just let it go.”


    Kara’s compelling argument was interrupted by Alana sticking her head through the door with an apologetic smile. “Miss Grant? Clark Kent called. He said thank you for the gift basket and asked if your meeting with him is still scheduled for three?”


    Lena watched the fight drain out of Kara along with some of her hope that Cat could be swayed. She slumped where she stood, no longer a proud alpha but one that had suffered tremendous trauma from being abandoned by the only family she had once had.


    “Of course you’re working with my cousin.” Kara sighed in resignation and officially gave up on the whole conversation. She turned to Lena with sad eyes that begged to leave and reached for her hand like she couldn’t make it out of there without her comfort. “I think we’re done here.”


    “Not by a long shot,” Cat informed them, her notebook back in hand as she sprang onto her feet to block their retreat. “Clark Kent is your cousin? He said he didn’t have any living relatives after that terrible accident.”


    “Yeah, I’m familiar with his version of events. It earns him a lot of sympathy, but that doesn’t make it true.” Kara’s sardonic tone couldn’t mask the depth of her pain, and the rawness of her voice halted Cat mid-step.


    “Alana,” Cat shrieked, startling half the staff on the floor and Kara, who winced at the volume. “Call Mr. Kent back. Tell him the interview is canceled. I’ve found someone else with a story that deserves to be told.”


    “What makes you think I’d tell you anything after you just antagonized me?” Kara asked, taken aback by Cat’s swift change in attitude as she tried to usher them back over to the couch.


    “Oh please, I barely ruffled you. Any journalist worth their salt would test you to see if you put your morals where your mouth is.” Cat’s flippant behavior alluded to how the mogul operated. She turned her critical eyes onto Lena and softened a bit as she set a small tape record on the table between them. “You picked a good one.”


    “Actually, Cat, she picked me.” Lena wasn’t shy about setting the record straight. She gazed in adoration at Kara as she leaned into her side. She also wrapped their arms together to cradle Kara’s hand between both of her own. “I was just fortunate enough to come to my senses before I tried to chase her off.”


    The love between them loosened some of the tension that hardened Kara’s posture, and she smiled down at Lena until Cat cleared her throat to remind them of her presence.


    “I want to know everything there is to know about Kara Danvers, and why Clark Kent has never once mentioned she existed.” Cat leaned forward to click record on her device and raised her brows expectantly as she sat back to ask her questions. “Who are you really, and why has Clark kept you a secret?”


    Kara took a deep breath and leaned forward so the recorder could pick up her voice clearly. “My name is Kara Danvers, but it wasn’t always.”


    Lena sat silently for well over an hour while Kara poured her heart out.


    Cat coaxed her mate into starting at the beginning and discussed the life Kara previously had when her parents were both alive. She gleaned information about the bond Kara once had with Clark, and how all of it took a turn on the night of the accident.


    Kara walked Cat through the wreckage of her childhood and the lonely, despondent years of being forgotten in foster care. She recalled listening to Clark on the radio for a source of comfort, and how she had been shut out of his life without fully realizing it.


    The deeper Kara delved into her history, the tighter she gripped at Lena’s hand. Tears welled in Kara’s eyes, and Lena sniffled quietly while Cat held back her own emotions to press on.


    They heard all about Eliza and Alex, and how stubborn and closed off Kara had become from it all. The struggles she endured to not only fit in at school, but in the new family that was desperate to accept her if only she allowed them the chance.


    Kara spared no harrowing detail, and even laughed at parts with self-deprecating humor. She painted a picture of how she had grown into the person she now was, and all of the trials and tribulations it took when she tried following in Alex’s footsteps.


    Things really turned around when Kara found her own path and established her pool cleaning business.


    “It’s not glamorous by any means, but I love it.” Kara’s pride shined through her smile, and she directed it towards Lena like she still couldn’t believe they were together. “If not for my business I would never have met Lena. Now I can’t imagine my life without her, or the kids, or even Andrea.”


    The sarcastic remark made it clear that despite their differences and all of the bullshit Andrea brought to their lives, Kara considered her family. For all intents and purposes, Andrea was off limits to Cat, but Clark wasn’t.


    “I was only a kid when I was cast aside.” Kara’s smile wobbled with emotion, and then her jaw firmed when Lena tightened her hold on her hand. “I was an adult when I realized we were nothing to each other except a bitter reminder that family isn’t who you share blood with; it’s who we choose to keep close.”


    Cat ruminated on that for a long moment and then steepled her fingers together to ask the most crucial question yet. “If you have proof of all this, why haven’t you come forward sooner?”


    “Because it stopped mattering to me when I became a Danvers. If Clark wanted me out of his life so badly, then I didn’t want to be part of his. Then he had the audacity to show up on our doorstep a few weeks ago and tell our kid he’s my cousin.” Kara’s lip curled in disdain and she gritted her teeth to suppress her anger. “He broke his silence, so now I’m breaking mine.”


    Cat smirked at that, and for the next half hour she browsed old text messages Kara had saved on her cell phone. She was also present for Kara’s call to Eliza where she requested her to send over proof so there was no doubt left in Cat’s mind.


    Scanned documents of Kara’s adoption were emailed over as soon as possible, along with the paperwork that confirmed the legal change of Kara’s last name. Eliza took the liberty to email over a few pictures of Clark visiting on the rare occasions he ever showed up, and a few very old pictures of Kara and Clark with their parents on vacation.


    “You’re being so brave divulging all of this, I hope you know that,” Lena whispered into the crook of Kara’s neck, and pressed sweet kisses to her throat to calm the quiver there. She needed Kara to understand that she was so immensely proud of her for no longer hiding away from her truths, and she kissed her without care as to what Cat thought.


    “I couldn’t do this without you, Lena. When I walked in here all I wanted to do was leave, but I’m glad I didn’t.” Kara pressed her forehead against Lena’s and took a moment to breathe in the fragrance of their love. “It’s time to let it all out, because I am sick of carrying this with me. I won’t let him weasel his way back into my life like he belongs there.”


    Lena took it upon herself to handle the negotiations with Cat over the exclusive rights to break the story after that. She made sure that Kara got the lion's share of the deal because she had suffered enough and this kind of breaking news would thrust CatCo back into the limelight.


    That ought to have been enough to satisfy everyone, except Cat Grant had one more thing to ask.


    “This little project of yours, the filtration system. Does it actually work?” Cat lowered her glasses down the bridge of her nose to peer at Kara.


    “Yes ma’am,” Kara uttered, reverting straight back to the humble and bashful alpha that had first walked into Cat’s office. “My friends and I have a fully functioning prototype that took us months to create. All we need is someone to believe in us.”


    Lena cleared her throat in offense and pursed her lips when Kara laughed.


    “Other than you,” Kara clarified with amusement, and shrugged at the peculiar way Cat observed them both. “I want to succeed on my own merit, not off the back of my brilliant and talented mate.”


    “Talk to Alana before you go. We’ll set up another meeting and you can show me the prototype. Bring your friends.” Cat flicked her fingers to dismiss them, but her smile revealed that she had developed a fondness for Kara in their short time together.


    Lena left the appointment in a bit of an optimistic daze. She trusted Cat Grant to present Kara’s story without over embellishing or sensationalizing it.


    Clark had several catchphrases about the importance of family that conflicted with the attitude he had towards Kara over the years. Viewers often solicited his advice about topics related to family values, and Lena knew Kara’s interview would have an impact on Clark’s platform.


    They would have to deal with that whenever the news broke, and Lena was a bit wary that the press coverage could bring out other old enemies – but she had no doubt someone like Clark Kent would have found a way to tell the world about Kara and put his own spin on their relationship. At least now he couldn’t lie, and Kara had the opportunity to share her story on her terms.

    Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 35

    Chapter Notes

    Lena was no stranger to the chaos that accompanied big achievements, especially when it pertained to kids, work, and exclusive events. Something, somewhere would inevitably go awry and throw everything into a tailspin. That was why she tried to prepare for it in advance. She had braced herself the moment they left Cat Grant’s office and hadn’t relaxed since.

    Kara went ahead and set up another meeting to go over her prototype, and within the week, she and her friends walked away with the mogul as their investor. All of the grueling hours and dedication on Kara’s personal project had finally paid off, and the joy they all experienced was nothing short of wonderful.



    Lena took pride in seeing her mate succeed, but that didn’t offset the paranoia that stubbornly persisted. For the next several days, she began each morning by checking social media to see if the Kara’s article was circulating all over the city yet.


    It confused Lena that Cat was sitting on the story instead of immediately publishing it, and she couldn’t fathom why.


    If it weren’t for the fact that they were in the middle of setting up a double celebration for Natty’s birthday and Sophia presenting as an omega, then Lena would have been an anxious mess.


    Kara’s exuberance was an infectious force that couldn’t be contained, and Lena was grateful that her mate kept her word and reached out to Andrea to help plan the whole thing.


    Sharing space with her ex was no easy task due to how obnoxiously overbearing Andrea could be at the best of times. Lena had dreaded the thought until Kara let slip that she had also called Bernardo and Lillian as back up.


    What could have been a simple planning session turned into several frantic days of posturing and arguing over the most basic things.


    Kara managed to stay out of the fray of it by handling the finer details and getting both of the girls the cakes they wanted.


    Lena took care of the guest list and turned a blind eye to the rest for the sake of her own sanity.


    Andrea, on the other hand, vetoed the catering company Lillian insisted they use, and then contacted the one she favored for all of her events at Obsidian North.


    Bernardo took issue with the minimalistic decorations his daughter preferred and hired a whole crew to string up balloon arches, lights and fabulous grand pinatas stuffed with candy. In retaliation, Andrea hired a few mermaids to hang out in the pool for Natty, and Lillian booked her own entertainment in the form of a petting zoo — a detail she neglected to inform anyone about until they started arriving.


    Lena’s wishful thinking of getting up early on Saturday morning to fool around before either of the parties started was ruined by the unmistakable bleating of sheep.


    “Is Natty already awake?” Kara blinked her eyes open to find Lena precariously close to licking the tip of her cock. The groan she exhaled was drowned out by neighing.


    “Those sounds are far too real to be one of her toys,” Lena grunted, her irritation lifting her off of the bed to tug the curtain aside. She glared into the expansive backyard to see her mother leading two alpacas across the grass, while several handlers tried to herd the rest of the animals through the back gate. “I might actually kill her today.”


    “Andrea or your mother?” Kara asked, already out of bed and half dressed as though she sensed she would be the one having to deal with whatever trouble was occurring.


    “Guess,” Lena intoned flatly, and stepped aside for Kara to see the wild animals flocking around Lillian like she was their shepherd. She saw the amusement lift the corners of her mate’s lips before Kara bit them into a tight line. “You’re actually happy my mother has done this, aren’t you?”


    “Should she have asked us first before doing this? Yeah, of course, and it’s not okay that she didn’t, but Lena, look! There’s a pony!” Kara stated with childlike glee. “You know Natty is going to love this.”


    “We’ll see how happy you are when you’re stuck cleaning up after it.” Lena’s grin caused Kara’s to falter and she grabbed the alpha by the chin to kiss her good morning. “Relax, I would never allow you to be roped into doing that, but you had better get out there to help pen them in or we’re going to have a bunch of toddlers running through poop in no time.”


    The sudden realization of how messy it could get rushed Kara into sprinting out of the room, and Lena watched her appear outside to take charge of the whole zoo.


    Guests wouldn’t be arriving until the afternoon, but the caterers would be due to show up soon. Lena texted Andrea to confirm that she was already on her way over with Bernardo, and
    that gave her a little under an hour to make herself presentable.


    The commotion outside hurried her through her normal routine at twice the speed. She had purchased a new dress for the occasion because all of her clothes were snug around her middle and she didn’t want to feel self-conscious while entertaining all of the parents. The flowy gown was loose everywhere else and made her bump the main feature.


    Lena knew that the dress would be one of Kara’s favorites from the moment she slipped it on and saw what it did to her figure. The fitted bust accentuated her tits and created a clear waistline in emphasis of her small baby bump.


    She just managed to finish zipping herself into the dress before Natty ran into the bedroom like something was chasing her.


    “Mommy, mommy, a pony! There’s a pony outside!” Natty carried a well-matted caticorn as she leapt into Lena’s arms. She used the height advantage to show her stuffed friend the whole menagerie of animals through the window. “Can he live in Sophia’s room?”


    Lena let out a soft exhalation that wasn’t quite a laugh. “Then where will your sister stay when she comes home from school?”


    “At Mama’s or in my room,” Natty pleaded, favoring logic instead of whining like other pups her age. “She’s gotten really good at sharing.”


    Lena smiled down at her four-year-old with a pang of sadness. Her littlest pup was showing all of the signs of growing up, and although she wouldn’t win the argument today, Lena had no doubts that Natty would challenge her in the future like Sophia did.


    “Why don’t we sign you up for some riding lessons first and you can learn all about ponies and how to take care of them?” Lena knew most equestrian programs wouldn’t take on such a young pup but she figured she could purchase some one-on-one lessons somewhere.


    Natty’s excitement was as high pitched as the shriek from Andrea when she stepped out of her Benz and into an unfortunate pile of manure.


    Lena knew better than to linger by the window as her ex stomped furiously across the yard towards Lillian, who cackled unapologetically over her filthy shoe.


    The day was going to be long, and it hadn’t even begun yet.


    Lena coaxed her daughter down the hall to her bedroom and rummaged through her closet for the perfect princess dress that Natty insisted upon wearing. The green and purple sparkly frill looked far more fairy-like than any princess Lena had seen, but Natty didn’t seem to mind as she swished the dress and giggled.


    “How would you like to have breakfast with your abuelo and grandmother before your friends arrive?” Lena asked, knowing the answer just from the way Natty gasped.


    It was a race downstairs as her four-year-old bolted out of her room to greet her grandparents. Natty almost bowled Bernardo over as she jumped into his outstretched arms.


    “Que linda, look at you, as regal as your grandmother,” Bernardo laughed, hoisting Natty high into his arms to show her off to Lillian.


    The sweet moment came to an end as Kara and Andrea elbowed each other get into the kitchen first. They only hesitated as they caught sight of Lena as she descended the stairs.


    Andrea’s scowl slipped right off her face and took her jaw along with it, and Kara’s eyes seemed to widen to twice their size.


    Kara nudged Andrea towards the mud room to clean off her shoe without uttering a word. She wiped her hands down her jeans with a dopey smile and peacocked like she wasn’t already Lena’s mate.


    Bernardo found his tongue first, and his moustache curled with his smile as he stepped forward with Natty clutched in his arms. “Lena, you look as radiant as ever. May I?”


    Lena blushed as she gave a curt nod and held Kara’s gaze while Bernardo rested his palm delicately on her baby bump. There was definitely movement, and he chuckled at the kick that pushed him away.


    “This one is going to be as feisty as my Sophia, and just as strong as their sire.”


    “Thank you, Bernardo,” Kara uttered with enough pride to choke Andrea into silence before she thought to ruin the mood. She tucked her thumbs into her belt loops to swagger over, and guided Lena into a seat at the dining table. “Lena, why don’t you sit down and catch up with everyone? I can take care of breakfast.”


    “We both can,” Andrea cut in, shocking everyone with how quick she rolled up her sleeves and grabbed a carton of eggs.


    Kara’s amusement was evident in how she raised her brows and motioned for Andrea to continue instead of insisting she get out of the way.


    Everyone took a seat to watch, and Lena bit her lip at the dual posturing taking place.


    Andrea tried to one-up Kara by cooking huevos rancheros. She moved around the kitchen like she still owned it, but there was a gracefulness to her concentration that wasn’t entirely born from rivalry. She wanted to impress Lena, and no doubt her father, but she was cooking for her kids and it actually brought a smile to Andrea’s face.


    Off to the side, Kara whipped up pancake batter and all the fixings for a special breakfast. She sliced up fruits and fried bacon, then cut thick slices of tomato and avocado to pair with Sophia’s favorite toast.


    When she noticed Lena staring, Kara went out of her way to flex as she flipped the pancakes in the pan, and earned a cheer from Natty when it landed.


    “Don’t take this the wrong way, but I didn’t realize Andrea was capable of cooking, let alone anything that smells delicious.” Lillian directed her remark to Bernardo, who seemed just as stunned by his daughter's talents.


    “When her mother was alive, she would help to prepare meals,” Bernardo divulged under his breath so as not to be heard by Andrea. “I’d hear them laughing from my office as they worked on family recipes, but the moment her mother passed, Andrea refused to step foot into the kitchen. I haven’t seen her cook in many years.”


    Lena blamed her hormonal state for the lump in her throat, and she was happy to be rid of it when Kara placed a pitcher of orange juice on the table. She sipped at the sweet and tart drink and tried not to consider how the loss Andrea had suffered had framed so much of her life.


    Though Kara finished plating all of her food, she held off on delivering it to the table to allow Andrea the chance to set hers down first. It was a small and simple act of kindness that went over Andrea’s head, but stuck in Lena’s heart.


    Andrea’s smile thinned around the edges when she realized her older daughters were missing, and frowned at their empty seats. “Where are Andy and Sophia? They should be down here by now.”


    “I’ll see what’s taking them so long while Kara makes me a plate with everything on it,” Lena uttered.


    She wasn’t joking because she felt ravenous from the scents in the air.


    The delectable sight of Kara with her shirt sleeves rolled up only added to the gnawing hunger she experienced. It took real self-restraint not to request the alpha accompany her upstairs. They would never return to eat if they managed to get a moment alone.


    Lena rose slowly if only to ensure Kara watched her run a hand across the swell of her middle, and she grinned at the way her mate’s eyes lidded with obvious longing. She wandered upstairs to find out what inevitable problem was taking place, and hesitated outside of Sophia’s room as she heard Andy’s long suffering sigh.


    “You need to keep your eyes open or I can’t do this.” Andy grumbled. “Do you want your lashes to clump?”


    Lena crept forward to peek through the open door, and watched as her eldest brandished a tube of mascara in front of Sophia’s face.


    “I don’t need your help. I can do this myself.” Sophia snapped back, though made no attempt to get out of the chair Andy had her perched on.


    “Sure, if you want to look like a panda. Why can’t you just trust me?” The jut of Andy’s lip was reminiscent of Lena's whenever she felt vulnerable.


    “I do,” Sophia grudgingly admitted, and then huffed as she tried to avoid Andy by tipping her chin up. “I just don’t want to look stupid in front of everyone. What if they laugh at me?”


    “I wouldn’t let you out of this room if you looked stupid.” Andy frowned down at her sister and gingerly began applying mascara in spite of Sophia’s rapid blinks.


    “It’s your party. If anyone makes you feel bad, tell me and I’ll throw cake in their face.”


    “You can’t do that,” Sophia scoffed, despite the smirk that formed on her lips at the thought of it.


    “Says who?” Andy challenged in true protective fashion and opened a little kit that contained her own lipsticks. She picked a light shade of pink that would complement Sophia’s complexion and applied the thinnest layer. She handed Sophia a piece of tissue to blot the excess off, and then turned her towards the mirror with a wry grin. “Nobody is going to make fun of you, especially when you look like this.”


    Sophia gaped at herself in the mirror, and then preened with the brightest smile.


    Lena could have stayed there all morning to witness the two of them bonding, but she didn’t want to intrude on their moment and snuck away while they finished getting ready.


    “They’ll be down in a minute,” Lena intoned as she returned to the kitchen to find Andrea tight-lipped and offended at Natty’s refusal to try her breakfast.


    “One bite?” Kara bargained, holding out a spoonful of the dish Andrea made.


    “Princesses eat cake.” Natty stubbornly crossed her little arms as if she expected to be treated like one for the day.


    Lena expected Kara to come up with some type of tale on the spot to persuade their four-year-old — but Andrea beat her to it.


    “I know plenty of princesses who love my huevos rancheros,” Andrea assured her out of desperation.


    Andy happened to slide into her chair at the right moment to pour herself juice and contribute to the story. “Yeah, she’s dated most of them, and I’m sure they always stay for breakfast.”


    Lillian inhaled her coffee over her granddaughter’s top tier snark, which Andy hadn’t delivered maliciously.

    “Andy,” Lena intoned, widening her eyes in silent warning before glancing at Andrea’s face, which relaxed as their oldest child scooped a bunch of eggs onto her plate.


    The teasing went over Natty’s head, who continued to sit in a posture of non-cooperation. She only stopped being on the defensive when Sophia walked into the room and tried to inconspicuously take her seat.


    Sophia wore a pale pink dress, which was drastically different from all of the outfits she used to wear as Andrea’s protégé. Her long skirt interfered with her ability to scoot her chair in, but that didn’t stop her from digging into the vegetarian options Kara prepared for her. Shimmers of pink highlighted her cheekbones and the lightest shades covered her eyelids to create a look of natural beauty.


    Lena expected to compliment her daughter and ended up crying instead. She fanned the tears away as she glanced around at her pups, who had each changed so much in just the space of a year.


    Kara noticed her emotional reaction and jumped into her usual role as a supportive parent and partner by handling the compliments. “Sophia, that dress is phenomenal and you look so pretty today.”


    “It’s a one-of-kind Balenciaga,” Andrea cut in, loading her plate up with Kara’s pancakes and more carbs than she would normally eat. “I have a lot of connections in the fashion world.”


    Sophia sat a little prouder with that knowledge and scooped up some of the huevos rancheros to add to her plate. “It’s beautiful and all of the omegas will be jealous it’s mine.”

    A few choice ways of retaliating had slipped into her head over the course of the day, especially whenever someone reached out to mention they had seen that Andrea was an invited guest on Clark’s new show.




    Lena could deal with any backlash and personal embarrassments that came about as a result of Andrea’s appearance, but it wasn’t fair to subject their kids to the pressure of being in the public eye – and that was to say nothing of how it would affect Kara.

     



    Andrea would most likely blame Kara for opening them all up to the media attention in the first place by publishing that article.



    “We’re all here and we’ve got your back.” Alex presented a united front with Sam as they both stood crossing their arms.

     

    Andy came into the room a short while afterward with her instrument case, backpack and an attitude. “Hey guys, why didn’t anyone tell me that Mom’s going on national TV this afternoon to humiliate Kara?”



    Lena should have hedged off any chance of this kind of confrontation with her daughter, and yet it had simply been pushed to the back of her mind. She approached her oldest child with an apologetic slant to her lips. “I’m sorry, Andy. I meant to tell you this morning so you wouldn’t be blindsided if anyone mentioned it to you at school.”

     

    “Yeah, well, that’s exactly what happened. Everyone in my theater class was talking about it and I couldn’t even get in touch with you to ask questions.” Andy held up her phone to display the texts she sent, all of which went unanswered due to Lena’s narrow fixation on setting up the surprise gathering.



    “Honestly, the only knowledge I have is that your mother is making an appearance. Kara is obviously the topic that Clark plans to discuss, but I can’t predict what his questions will be or how your mother will respond. If she does any kind of damage, you can take the day off from school tomorrow, and we’ll probably have to pick your sister up for an unplanned two-week vacation just to avoid everyone.” Lena pushed her chin out, flattened her lips and shrugged as if unbothered by the circumstances.

     


    No one could be fooled by her behaviors though — not with how she flinched in response to hearing the music at the start of Clark’s talk show.



    “Oh shit, it’s starting,” Sam noted as she reached out to take Natty’s backpack and settle the little one at her kiddie table where a plate of fruit and crackers waited for her.



    “Mama’s on TV!” Natty pointed with the cutest look of confusion on her face and a happy bob of her head as she plucked a strawberry from her plate. “I don’t want to watch this. Can I see Mermaid Tales?”



    “After the show,” Andy promised and perched herself on the ottoman to brace herself for whatever was about to transpire.


    Sam and Alex took a seat at the furthest end of the couch and left the rest for Kara and Lena to get situated.



    Nobody said a word as Lena lifted the remote to turn the volume up, but the tension in the room was palpable the moment the camera panned to Clark’s smiling face.


    “Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for joining me this evening for my brand new show Chatting with Clark. Some of you may have noticed I’ve made quite a few headlines recently but stick with me and I promise you’ll get the answers you’ve all been waiting on.”



    Clark laughed it off, but there were stress lines to his smile that couldn’t be hidden in 4K. He swung his arm out as he walked over to the desk set up for him and indicated Andrea while the crowd cheered and clapped.



    “My first guest tonight is no stranger to making headlines, either. You may know her as the alpha who built the first biofuel vehicle. Please put your hands together for Andrea Rojas.”


    Andrea ate up the attention with a wide grin and ran her hand absently down the bow on her perfect Givenchy blouse as she waved to the crowd. She took her seat to face Clark and crossed her leg to rest her hands on her knee. “Thank you for having me here, Clark. It’s an honor to be your very first guest on the show.”


    “Kiss ass,” Sam griped, then stiffened as she remembered the kids were in the room. “Sorry, that was rude of me.”


    “No, you were right.” Andy folded her arms across her chest, which seemed to mimic Kara, who also sat stoically awaiting the worst.


    Lena consciously chewed on her own grievances and swallowed them down as she placed a comforting hand on her mate’s thigh.




    Andrea had never understood the difference between bad press and good press, because as long as her name was out there, it generated income. In her ex’s mind, that was still a win, though Lena worried how low Andrea was willing to stoop in her pursuit of revenge.


    “I’m sure it came as no surprise that I reached out to you. After all, we share a certain someone in common, don’t we?” Clark’s joyful demeanor was still rigid as he held Andrea’s stare with a fixed grin that refused to waver.


    The crowd fell into an expectant hush, and Lena held her breath as Andrea blinked coyly and relaxed her posture to show how at ease she was being broadcast into every home across the country.


    This was it. The sickening moment they all knew was coming, no more than three minutes into the airing.



    Andrea’s smirk gave nothing away as she raised her brows and kept her voice perfectly neutral with charm. “If you mean Cat Grant, I promise you that my appearance in several of her articles comes down to my impeccable taste in fashion.”


    The audience laughed at Andrea’s playful comment, but Clark didn’t. He pushed his glasses so far up the bridge of his nose that he almost bent the frames, but he managed to keep his smile intact, even though he showed too many teeth for it to be genuine.


    “Wait,” Andy muttered in confusion, and glanced at the adults to confirm that she had heard her sire deflect the question with relative ease.


    “Is she fucking with him?” Alex blurted, too stunned to censor herself as she gawked at Andrea’s smug face.




    “Language,” Kara hissed and thumped Alex on the arm hard enough to slosh wine up the side of her glass.




    “Oh, now we definitely need snacks,” Sam intoned and poked Andy in the ribs to get her to pass over a bag of chips.



    The sound of rustling died down the second Clark straightened his tie, and Andy shoved a few pieces of popcorn into her mouth to chew anxiously.

     



    “I have no doubt it’s your fashion sense that keeps those reporters at CatCo coming back for more,” Clark chuckled with a white knuckled grip on his mug of coffee. He tried to appear calm and amused as he cast his gaze out to the crowd to loudly clarify, “But that’s not who I meant. For those of you at home who aren’t already aware, the self-proclaimed Queen of Media dropped a story to shock the nation on the subject of my cousin. But I don’t have to ask you who Kara Danvers really is. Isn’t that right, Andrea? You already know her as the alpha who’s dating your ex-wife.”




    That tidbit of information caused a collective gasp from the audience and Clark’s smile was finally real as he reclined in his seat.




    Andrea, on the other hand, didn’t react at all. She raised her brows once the hushed murmuring died down and leveled Clark with a look Lena had come to see as a warning of antagonism.



    “And here I thought you’d invited me on to talk about my latest piece of tech, which is due to hit the market next month. Keep an eye out for it because it’s going to revolutionize your life.” Andrea addressed the audience instead of Clark like they were her fans and flashed a grin when a round of applause went up.



    “What’s happening?” Andy asked in disbelief and laughed at the dumbfounded way Clark left his mouth agape. “She just ignored his bait twice in a row.”




    “She’s figuring out which of his buttons to push to get the best reaction out of him,” Kara stated with a soft sort of shock that brought her forward to stare at the screen. She propped her elbows on her knees and blindly grabbed a handful of popcorn out of Andy’s bowl.

     

     

    “That’s another hot topic I’d love to discuss right after we chat about the alpha of the hour. Kara Danvers. As many of you know by now, Kara is an entrepreneur who runs a pool cleaning business. Her customers say she’s a happy and positive person, but is there a dark side to Kara that CatCo failed to expose? We’ll be chatting about that next. Stick with us and get the complete story.” Clark postured for the camera with one of his side-grins, which exposed just half of his teeth and brought out the dimples in his cheeks.

     


    The cut to the commercial break gave him the chance to re-group with Andrea and force the conversation in the direction he intended it to go.



    The issue was that it would take a lot longer than five minutes to get control of someone like Andrea.




    Lena wondered about all of her ex’s motives in taking on the spotlight and waited with bated breath for some clarity.

     

     

    The music for Clark’s live show came back on, and Andrea still looked as poised as ever. She clasped her hands in her lap and flashed her flawless smile to the cameras without so much as a touch of anxiety.

     

     

    Kara seemed to be grinding her teeth together, and Lena reached out to touch her knee as Clark started in again.



    “Kara Danvers has been described as an optimist, an innovator, and a good partner – but the truth is she’s one of the most negative people I’ve ever met. She’s had quite an impact on my life, which is why I was forced to separate myself from her and start fresh. The reason you haven’t heard her name until recently is because I was forced to cut her out of my life – not callously, but because I was at risk. She was a troubled youth, and it’s obvious to me she’s become a troubled adult.”

     

     

    The outright lies had the audience focused on Clark to the exclusion of Andrea, but he made a fatal mistake by including her in that part of his narrative.


    “Wouldn’t you agree, Miss Rojas? According to my private investigations, Kara pursued your wifeduring a period of separation between you. It’s my understanding that you hoped to repair the marriage, and Kara not only went out of her way to drive a wedge in the family, but she also destroyed the claim on your wife’s neck.”



    The hurt that surfaced on Andrea’s face would have convinced anyone of the truth of Clark’s story, and Lena panicked that he had managed to hit on all the topics that would get the emotional reaction he desired.



    Kara stopped intaking breath and stared directly ahead at the television.

     

     

    “You’re adding embellishments that have no basis in reality,” Andrea countered with a small sniff and a lift of her brows. “We had been divorced for years at that point and I was also seeing someone else. Kara isn’t a homewrecker, plain and simple.”

     

    Clark’s bright smile gradually dimmed and his jaw muscles jumped from the way his teeth clenched in anger. It took a lot of self-control not to let his friendly mask slip, and he shuffled some papers on his desk with a bit of a laugh.



    “I understand this must be difficult for you to discuss. As an alpha with my own pup, I can only imagine the pain of being replaced by someone who’s unfit to raise my child, but that is what’s happened here, isn’t it?” Clark stared Andrea right in the eye while he twisted the proverbial knife to cut his way under her skin. “My sources say that Kara Danvers has already filed for guardianship, and when you found out, she assaulted you for speaking out about it.”



    “Bullshit,” Andy coughed into her hand and then ducked like she expected to be rightfully reprimanded for swearing. When it didn’t happen, she turned to see the discomfort on Kara’s face and the panic that was all over Lena’s features. “He’s lying, right?”



    Lena’s first instinct was to agree, because she had spent so many awful years covering for Andrea’s terrible behavior.



    Andrea had earned that punch from Kara — and not just because of the devastation she caused their family, but for what she had done to Nia in the process.


    Kara braved the conversation without making any excuses for herself, and leaned forward to clasp Andy by the shoulder with a truly contrite expression. “No, he’s not lying about everything. Clark found a way to slip in a kernel of truth to make the most impact. I’m not proud of how I handled myself at the time, but I did strike your sire once in anger. I owe you the details of why it occurred, but I would prefer to sit down with you when Natty has gone to bed so I can answer any questions you might want to ask.”


    Andy looked upset by the news but instead of shrinking away from Kara, she turned her sharp eyes onto Lena and picked at the sleeve of her hoodie. “Did she at least deserve it?”



    “As a parent, I’m supposed to say that nobody deserves to be hit, and I don’t condone violence. But yes. In this case, she really did.” Lena hated that they were having to rehash something so volatile, but Andy was smart enough to know that her other mother would never have tolerated being around Kara if she truly held lingering animosity over the fight.



    “So that’s why she ran off to Mexico.” Andy pieced it all together with a sage nod that made her seem wiser beyond her years. “It was because you bruised her ego.”



    “And her lip,” Alex added with true sibling pride that earned her a smack from Sam.



    “Shh, or we’ll miss what she says next,” Sam berated her girlfriend, and then offered Natty some of her chips when the little one heard the bag crinkle.



    On screen, Andrea had draped her arm over the back of her chair to posture confidently. She raised her chin with all the arrogance of someone who knew their legal team outmatched her opponent’s and let a cocky smile slip onto her face.


    “I’m not sure who your sources are, Clark, but I think you need to find better ones. It’s true that Kara has filed for guardianship of my girls, but what you're failing to report is that it’s with my blessing.” Andrea looked straight into the camera as she spoke, and for a second, Lena thought she had fallen asleep and the whole day was a dream.



    Kara unlatched her jaw and sat forward like she couldn’t believe her own ears.




    Sam gave herself whiplash from turning toward Lena to gawk at her in surprise.



    It was too soon to say if Andrea meant it, but Lena doubted her ex would ever utter something like that on live TV if she didn’t plan to stand behind her statements.




    “Your blessing,” Clark sputtered, his laughter a little unhinged as he leaned across his desk to glare at Andrea. “C’mon, you can’t really expect us to believe that?”

     

      

    “Why not?” Andrea challenged with the same fiery defiance that always surrounded her before she went in for the kill. “Kara and I have a good co-parenting relationship. We even participated in the Family Day activities this year at my daughter’s school to show my children they have two alphas in their life to look up to now. I’m sure there’s footage of it somewhere on the internet, and if there isn’t, there will be now.”


    Andrea pulled out her phone. With a few fast taps, she turned the screen toward the nearest camera so it could zoom in on the video Andy had taken.


    Andrea played it for the folks at home, and someone on set projected the image for the audience, who cracked up at the sight of Kara having to carry Andrea mid-way down the field.


    “One little video doesn’t really capture someone’s true character,” Clark disputed with bitter resentment he aimed at Andrea for refusing to play along.


    “I suppose you’d have to say that, given all of the clips currently circulating on social media from when you crashed my daughter’s party this weekend.” Andrea’s cavalier approach disarmed the audience, and she flicked her gaze over Clark with disdain curling her lip. “Don’t get me wrong, I understand wanting to protect your family, but you practically discarded yours into the foster system. It must have been horrible when you and Kara both lost your parents in that tragic accident. It also must have come as quite a shock to discover your aunt and uncle left Kara a very hefty trust fund. From what I uncovered, they appointed you control over it. Drained it dry, didn’t you?”

     

     

    “I have no idea what you’re talking about,” Clark bluffed with a redness to his face from outrage. He used a handkerchief to wipe sweat from under his glasses as he came up with an excuse to explain away his guest’s angle. “It’s obvious you’ve come on my show to humiliate me and lie to the nation just to protect your own image.”

     

     

    “I came on your show to expose you as a self-centered ass who shouldn’t be offering anyone advice about family problems or preaching about the importance of honesty and integrity. You have none. Good luck with your show, Mr. Kent. I have a feeling you’re going to need it.” Andrea slid up from her chair and smiled for the audience as she strutted down the center aisle to the exit.

     

     

    “She defended me. She actually defended me.” Kara blinked at the television, too baffled to make sense of the situation.


    Sam poked a straw into a juice box for Natty, who was too busy playing on her tablet to have paid attention to the live show. “I honestly can’t believe it. My guess is she’s going to expect some kind of big favor in return.”


    Lena feared that her best friend had the most logical take on Andrea’s defense of Kara, though she didn’t want to be that pessimistic.




    “What kind of favor?” Alex asked warily before anyone could volunteer any other explanations of the bizarre and out-of-character behavior.




    “Who knows with her?” Sam whispered with soft eyes that traveled back to Lena and offered her comfort.




    Lena’s phone pinged with a lot of texts all at once — and the most important message was from her ex.


    “It’s Andrea. She’s stopping by on her way home. I suppose we’ll find out if she wants a favor soon enough.”




    “I have to give her credit either way,” Alex reflected, curiously sliding her eyes over to Kara’s stunned face. “She dug up some real dirt on Clark. It might be worth checking her sources for more information about your trust fund. If Andrea found any publicly available documents, Clark committed a crime by depriving you of your inheritance.”


    Kara stood up to shake out all of the tension and jitters that must have been weighing on her throughout the day. “I don’t care about the money as much as I care about my reputation. Andrea had my back today. I would happily do anything I can to repay her.”


    “Let’s not get ahead of ourselves,” Lena cautioned with true worry about her mate’s generous and kind nature being exploited.




    She had every reason to be concerned about Kara feeling indebted to her ex wife. Their entire relationship had been rocky up until the past weeks of family bonding time, and while Lena wanted to believe everyone was capable of change, she also knew her ex wife on a deeper and more intimate level.

    Andy grabbed a packet of sour patch kids and chewed some of the blue ones in between imparting her own wisdom on her sire. “Mom has done some exceptionally shitty things, so I wouldn’t take on the pressure of feeling like you owe her anything. She’s part of this family and that’s enough. We’re all here to support her if she needs us.”


    “Andy, you make us proud.” Sam popped open a diet soda and sipped at the bubbles before they went everywhere. “Seriously, even though we’re a dysfunctional bunch, at least we’ve raised some amazing kids.”




    For the next hour, they chatted about future family plans that included an upcoming rock concert that Andy wanted to attend with Kara.



    It pushed all worries out of Lena’s mind for a short while until she received another text from Andrea asking her to come outside:


    Hey, I’m parked out front. I seem to have sprained my ankle, and to be perfectly honest, I just wanted a moment to talk with you privately. Would you mind coming to me?


    “Andrea just texted. She says she only has a minute and wanted to speak to me specifically, so I guess I’ll be right back.” Lena scrunched her brows together in confusion as she glanced to Kara, who must also have been questioning what topics might come up in a private discussion.



    Nevertheless, Lena had only one way of finding out and no one discouraged her from doing that.



    “It’s better if you talk to her alone because she’ll be more forthcoming about any ulterior motives with you.” Sam waved her off as they all headed into the kitchen to prep dinner.


    “Just let me know what she has in mind,” Kara muttered with the unease of someone who had accepted a deal on terrible terms.


    Lena pulled on a light jacket and nodded as stepped out of the house. There was nothing she would discuss with Andrea that she wouldn’t also share with the rest of the family, and her ex was likely aware of that.



    She walked down the front steps and slipped into Andrea’s newest car — a white Lamborghini with custom details and buttery soft leather that Lena melted into as she glanced over at Andrea’s serious face.


    “Are you okay? What did you want to talk about?” Lena searched her ex’s solemn blue eyes for any trace of deception.



    She exhaled a little sigh of relief upon realizing that Andrea wasn’t in any kind of mood to hold anything over their heads.




    Andrea took a shaky breath and let it go. She sounded like a balloon leaking air as she laid her thoughts and feelings out.


    “I wanted you to know that I appreciate your recent efforts to make me a part of this family again, Lena. I realized in Mexico that I’ve spent years running away from the idea of families, and that was utterly foolish of me. I value our family over everything else, and I’ll never let anyone hurt you or the girls ever again. And yes, that includes me. I owe our kids an apology, and I wanted to say that I’m sorry I ever hurt you.”


    Lena broke eye contact and twisted her fingers in discomfort. She believed those sentiments since they had been backed up by actions, but she wasn’t ready to address Andrea’s apology yet. Instead she focused on what she was grateful for as she lowered her voice to the softest whisper of gratitude.



    “Thank you for this afternoon. You saved all of us from an even bigger and more damaging media storm, and I know that Kara is especially thankful for how you protected her good name.”


    Mentioning Kara didn’t elicit the same kind of reaction that she had become accustomed to receiving from Andrea.



    Lena breathed in nothing but the scents of calm reassurances from her ex — striking and similar to the pheromones Andrea had given off in moments when she used to hold her.


    Andrea could deceive anyone in board rooms but she had one little tell of truthfulness— the way she calmed the restless waters of her eyes until they were placid and furrowing her brow. “Kara has shown me grace at times I didn’t deserve it, and I felt this was one way to atone for all I’ve done.”



    “We had already forgiven you, Andrea, and it was actually nice having you here this weekend to help with Sophia’s party.” Lena truly meant that and conveyed it through her own pheromones, which were more open and gentler than they had been in a long time when dealing with her ex.




    Andrea had no reason to become suddenly anxious or face Lena with more apologies in her eyes. “Well, I’m here for you and the girls no matter what you need.”


    They both could have choked on their emotions if Andrea wasn’t fast in pulling a folded piece of paper from her pocket.


    “There’s one more thing I wanted to tell you. In preparation for my meeting with Clark, I did extensive research. Actually, I hired one of the most notable and most expensive investigators to delve deeper into Kara’s history. He didn’t turn up anything questionable or unsavory.”



    Andrea clutched the slip of paper between her middle and forefinger as though reluctant to pass it over.




    “Then what do you have in your hand?”



    Lena had been through a lot in a twenty-four hour period and she already had the notion that this was another surprise she wouldn’t want. And she happened to be correct in her assumptions.


    “There’s an omega who has been looking for Kara on social media. These are her contact details. My investigator spoke to her personally. She’s been wanting to get in touch with Kara for years. From the way things sound, this omega was in love with Kara, and I very much believe that love was reciprocated. I thought I would give this to you so you could make the decision whether or not to pass this info along to Kara. I doubt she’s going to want it, but it seems like they were separated under less than ideal conditions, so this may be their only shot to meet again.”




    Andrea stuck out her fingers with the slip of paper, and it crinkled as it transferred hands.

    Chapter 38

    Chapter Notes

    Keeping secrets from a partner was never a good idea, but Lena couldn’t bring herself to pass on the contact information that Andrea provided.



    One major issue was that the details conflicted with what Lena knew to be true about her mate.



    Kara had never been with an omega outside of Lena — or at least that was what she had claimed from the very start of their relationship.



    It would have been a normal response to Google the name on the piece of paper and do a little digging of her own. Instead, Lena kept it creased  and stored it in a book that she tucked on a shelf inside her home office.



    Kara never pried through her things, and concealing it seemed the easiest way to keep it safe while Lena deliberated over what to do.

    Unfortunately, time wasn’t on her side. Lena knew that the second the information passed hands in Andrea’s Lamborghini. She should have handed it straight to Kara that night, but their friends and family were present, and emotions were already high from Andrea’s take-down of Clark.


    Lena promised herself that she would sleep on it, and then inform Kara in the morning before they dropped Andy off at school.



    Waiting any longer than that jeopardized the trust between them.

     

    Lena settled into bed hours later with the calm reassurance that everything would be fine by morning.



    She didn’t expect to find herself tormented and wide awake while Kara slept soundly beside her.


    Kara wouldn’t deceive her or build the foundations of their relationship on an unnecessary lie.



    So why did Lena feel threatened by this unknown omega?



    Lena mulled it over while she studied the soft lines of her mate’s face.



    She wouldn’t hold Kara’s past against her, no matter who she had previously dated, although that dredged up the realization that Lena didn’t know much of anything about Kara’s exes.


    Why was that?



    The cynical side of Lena wanted to tear open old wounds and betrayals from Andrea, but that wasn’t fair or appropriate.



    Kara deserved the chance to explain herself just as much as Lena deserved to have an honest discussion without letting her pregnancy hormones dictate her emotions.


    Their whole relationship had been a whirlwind of love and chaos from outside forces, mostly due to Andrea’s drama.



    Perhaps Lena should have asked more questions at the start instead of being swept up in the romance and falling so hard for Kara.



    No matter what happened, Lena couldn’t bring herself to regret a single moment of their history.



    Lena soothed herself with the knowledge that Andrea had found nothing untoward in Kara’s past, and that the person she loved was exactly who she had always claimed to be. She wrapped herself up in that knowledge to finally drift off into a troubled dream.


    The next morning, she woke with Kara’s arms around her, and everything was right in the world for a blissfully long minute of cuddling.



    The sound of their alarm jarred Lena back to reality, and her heart followed the tempo of the awful noise as it battered within her chest.


    It felt wrong to relax in the warmth of Kara’s embrace, and Lena narrowly dodged the hot press of Kara’s lips as she sleepily murmured, “Good morning.”


    “I hid something from you,” Lena blurted out from guilt and saw the shock register on Kara’s face like she doused her with ice water. “I’m sorry. I panicked. That’s not an excuse. I just thought it would be easier to tell you this morning, and I think I might have been wrong.”


    “What did you hide?” Kara asked, pinching her lips together in a way that showed small lines of worry. She peeled the blankets back so they could both sit up and turned towards Lena to look her in the eyes. The panic she found there kept her visibly on edge, but she carefully reached out to clasp Lena’s cheek and tried to reduce Lena’s stress with calm claim pheromones.


    “Whatever it is Lena, you can tell me.” Kara spoke with a steadfast resolution that she would be able to handle it no matter what. “I just need you to breathe because all of this stress isn’t good for you or the baby.”

     

    “Last night, Andrea gave me the contact details of an omega who has been looking for you for years,” Lena explained with a contrition that even changed her pheromones to an apologetic scent. “When she did some digging into Clark, her investigator came across this omega who said she dated you. She’s been searching for you with the hopes of reconnecting. I wasn’t trying to keep that from you, and I haven’t looked into her yet either – but I was tempted. Not because I’m worried about where your heart lies, but because you’ve always said I was the only omega you’d ever been with—”

    “You are,” Kara stated with so much conviction that it was impossible to take it as anything but the truth. “I have no idea who this woman is, but she’s either seriously confused, or has me mistaken for someone else. My only serious relationship was with a beta I met in college. Yeah, I loved her a lot, but it didn’t work out. I hated it at the time, but I couldn’t be more grateful now. If I had ended up with her, I never would have met you. You’re my only omega.”

    “I had better be,” Lena sniffled, not nearly as playfully as she had hoped to sound when Kara was looking at her with such devotion.



    She felt stupid for ever worrying and instinctively pressed her face into Kara’s shoulder to nuzzle at her mate’s claim.



    “I’m not about to piss off the mother of my kids, especially when I hope to have more.” Kara raised Lena’s chin with the tips of her fingers to kiss her sweetly on the lips. “Now, do you want breakfast or a shower first? We have about twenty minutes before Andy is awake.”

     

    “Shower,” Lena intoned with a meaningful sweep of her gaze down Kara’s torso to where the rest of her mate was hidden by the sheets. “On the condition that you’ll join me, of course.”


    “Well, who am I to deny the love of my life anything?” Kara mused with a smitten grin that didn’t detract from the fact that her eyes were definitely on Lena’s tits.


    The light flirtation eased them back into their usual routine and brought with it a comforting sense of normalcy.



    Lena padded into the bathroom to start the day, and attempted to put to rest all of her fears of an old love swooping in to steal Kara away from her.



    She sent a coquettish glance over her shoulder to make sure her mate was following and tried not to smirk at the sight of Kara already on her feet and at half-mast.



    It soothed Lena’s omega in a way that nothing else could, and she played it coy by biting her lip and stepping under the hot spray first.



    It might have been a little premature to declare the situation a non-issue, but Lena could think of nothing else as Kara stepped into the shower behind her with an appraising rumble.



    Kara dragged light fingers up her arms, and Lena whimpered from the warm press of her mate’s aroused tip against her thigh.
