    “You guys thought of absolutely everything. This is the perfect shirt to wear, and I’ll need this fancy box of tissue for when I cry a lot of happy tears. Thank you.” Kara lifted the tissue box and grinned at the joy on Natty’s face.

     

    Andy stopped by Lena to give her a one-armed hug, and seemed to stand taller under Kara’s praise. She flashed a toothy grin, and Lena chuckled when her mate fist-bumped Andy as a thank you.

     

    It was the kind of sweet moment she wished Sophia had been present to experience, and for a hormonal moment, Lena teared up due to her absence.

     

    By sheer luck, nobody seemed to notice—probably because Kara was in the process of trying to get everyone out the door in the politest way possible.

     

    “Are you guys ready to go have fun with your grandmother?” Kara asked somewhat exclusively to Natty to rile the little one up. It worked in her favor, and Natty flung her arms up with an excited shriek and turned her face expectantly to Lillian.

     

    “Yeah, let’s go!” Natty yelled, and tried to command Lillian to get moving by bopping Frederico’s head to make him nod in agreement.

     

    Andy snorted at her sister’s antics, but her own excitement was far more subdued, despite how she took a step toward the door.

     

    “Well, we don’t have to leave just yet. I’m a little parched,” Lillian intoned as she smacked her lips together. She glanced toward the living room with raised brows and angled herself like she was about to walk off.

     

    “I’ll grab you a bottle of water for the road.” Lena deadpanned and pointed toward the kitchen. She sensed the trouble they were in from the way her mother huffed at the suggestion, and shot Kara a silent I told you so look.

     

    “This is the thanks I get for spending quality time with my grandchildren?” Lillian articulated like an actress on Broadway and made a grand sweeping gesture like she had never been more offended in her entire life. “I drove all the way here, and you can’t even offer your own mother a mint julep or a Moscow mule?”

     

    “You just said you drove here,” Lena hissed, keenly aware of the impressionable ears listening to Lillian’s every word. “Why would I ply you with alcohol and then give you my children to transport twenty minutes away?”

     

    “Technically, Harold drove,” Lillian muttered under her breath and flicked her eyes onto Kara, as if she knew the alpha would be easier to sway with her machinations. “I thought it would be wise to have someone on hand in case you wanted to have a small celebration with your family before leaving for the event.”

     

    Kara’s wide eyed panic said she had been thoroughly unprepared for Lillian’s tactics, and Lena stepped in to shield her mate from the crafty manipulations.

     

    The only issue was that someone rattled the door, and everyone swung their heads towards it just as Andrea walked in unannounced with several people trailing at her back.

     

    “This is why you wanted me to leave, so you can host her?” Lillian accused amid the clear confusion everyone else shared.

     

    The scandalized scent that covered Lillian brought a smirk to Andrea’s lips, and she strode forward like they were old friends and not active enemies. “Lillian, a pleasure as always. You don’t look a day over eighty.”

     

    “I’m only sixty-three—” Lillian sputtered in outrage, and from the vibrant shade of her face, it was clear that she was absolutely incensed by Andrea’s remark.

     

    “What are you doing here, Andrea, and why have you brought guests?” Lena cut in before her mother had a conniption.

     

    She caught Andy out the corner of her eye valiantly trying not to laugh behind Kara, who immediately went into damage control mode.

     

    Lena couldn’t hear exactly what her mate was saying, but the gist of it knocked ten years off of her mother’s age.

     

    “Kara invited me to the launch party, and I thought she might appreciate having my team of stylists on hand to help her get ready.” Andrea motioned for everyone to step forward with a snap of her fingers.

     

    There was a make-up artist, her hair stylist and a sassy-looking beta in a flamenco shirt that held multiple outfits in separate garment bags slung over his arm.

     

    “Oh, that’s kind of you, but I don’t need—uh— all of this.” Kara’s usual tact was lacking as she glanced at the trio of people all sizing her up like their next pet project. She swallowed audibly and tensed her jaw to try to seem less intimidated. “I bought a new suit, and Andy picked me out this beautiful shirt.”

     

    “You don’t get on the front cover of Alpha Industries looking like you dressed yourself. Trust me, I’ve been featured five times in the past year alone.” Andrea’s humble brag wasn’t nearly as noxious as her usual, self-obsessed posturing. She leveled Kara with a look and dropped her voice in a rare display of modulation, so she didn’t embarrass her in front the kids. “My team won’t do anything unless you agree to it, and I’ll keep my own opinions to myself, unless you specifically ask for them.”

     

    Kara hesitated for a split second as she glanced at Lena, and then pulled herself up to her full height with a decisive glimmer in her eye. “Right, okay. Let’s get ready for the biggest night of my life.”

     

    “We’ll take the spare room,” Andrea stated, more to put Lena’s mind at ease than to call the shots as she ushered everyone upstairs and out of the way.

     

    Lena remained on tenterhooks for the duration of time that Andrea was upstairs with Kara.

     

    She placated her mother with a drink while Andy told them all about her day and the new friend she made in art class.

     

    In spite of experiencing one interruption after the next, Lena was in a good mood when she hustled upstairs to get herself ready for the event.

     

    On one of the many occasions when Kara was working, Lena had purchased a fabulous dress from a local boutique.

     

    She popped into the shower alone, and didn’t have the chance to lament Kara’s absence due to lacking time.

     

    She hurried through her routine, and experienced a tingle of excitement as she slipped on her couture evening gown.

     

    The floor length, deep blue fabric was like a twilit sky with appliques of gold diaphanous wings that made her look celestial. Her loose wavy hair worked with the gown, and she used a single pearl clip to hold some of it place.

     

    Lena finally picked up her suede and leather clutch and slipped her feet into a pair of Aquazurra velvet pumps to complete the outfit.

     

    Andrea’s stylist whistled as she walked down the hall, and Lena tossed him a wide grin as she tried to step into the spare room.

     

    “Not yet!” Andrea complained, squeaking through the door and directing Lena to the stairs with a hand on her back. “Kara will be down in a second. You’ll ruin the whole reveal if you see her before she’s finished.” She retracted her fingers at a delay and glanced over Lena’s attire with a heat of possessive familiarity in her eyes.

     

    Those kinds of looks had once been a real problem in their off-and-on again relationship. They had caused a lot of confusion because Lena interpreted Andrea’s reactions to her own desirability as evidence of lingering love. So much had changed over the past few years, and now Lena just chuckled at Andrea’s manner of standing close to her. She even fixed the twisted knot of Andrea’s tie with an amused smile tugging at her lips.

     

    “It was kind of you to arrange for your stylists to see Kara tonight.” Lena separated from her ex to glance back at the door to the spare bedroom. Her excitement was a feeling, sparkling and bubbling inside of her like the champagne she wouldn’t be drinking.

     

    Kara sauntered out in a grain de poudre tuxedo with her hair tied back and woven in a side-braid.

     

    Lena went a little dopey and speechless, her lips parting and pulse picking up speed as she drank in the confident swagger of her mate dressed to the nines. She made some small, whimpery sound that Andrea pretended not to hear or judge, even if Lena could sense the tension radiating off of her ex.

     

    Kara’s reaction wasn’t subtle, either, and she paused mid-step to take Lena in as her entire face lit up at the sight of her.

     

    The alpha’s grin widened along with her eyes, and she quickened her step to rush over and sweep Lena into her arms.

     

    Lena never expected to be lifted off the ground, or feel so thoroughly charmed that she giggled.

     

    “God, look at you,” Kara rasped as she finally settled Lena back onto her feet but kept her hands on her waist to hold her close. She gawked at Lena, evidently stunned and thoroughly elated, with pheromones that were heavily flirtatious. “You’re sensational. If you weren’t already pregnant–”

     

    Andrea cleared her throat before she overheard anything else, and made the snap decision to herd her team back into their vehicles with a wave of her hand. “All right people, let’s get moving. I want to say goodbye to my kids before we have to leave.”

     

    Lena took a moment to rest her forehead against Kara’s and breathe, but it was a short-lived reprieve from the chaos that came afterward. Natty squeezed in between the legs of all of Andrea’s stylists and latched onto Kara before it was time to depart. Andy looked up sharply from her music and texting, and came over to hold the door for everyone.

     

    On their way out, Andy nodded her approval to Kara, kissed Lena on the cheek, and threw her arm over Andrea’s shoulder in an unprompted hug.

     

    Lillian waved them off with an actual linen handkerchief, which Lena suspected she brought along just for the theatrics. “Oh, Kara, you look wonderful! Goodbye, you three! Have a fabulous time!”

     

    Everyone climbed into their different vehicles, and within the half hour, they were arriving at the launch. Cat Grant’s events tended to be exclusive affairs for highly influential guests, and the open bar made for a party that was non-family friendly. The venue was the most expensive resort in the area, and one of the places where Kara’s new filtering system was already installed.

     

    At any other party or charity gala, Lena would have soothed Kara’s nerves with physical contact. This time, all she could was hold her mate’s hand for fear of wrinkling her flawless tux or shirt.

     

    The spotlight would be on Kara all night, and Lena’s energies went into fussing over her while they were in the limo. She brought along breath mints, a mini lint roller, a stain remover pen, packs of tissues, and a lot of other emergency necessities in her purse.

     

    “Boy, I’m grateful you came prepared,” Kara breathed while she peered at the contents of the bag. “You’re always thinking of me. You know, I never thought I would have a mate who considers my needs on a daily basis and even takes the time to do little things like this. Having you in my corner has changed my life, Lena. I want you to know that you’re the motivation behind everything I do – you and our kids.”

     

    Lena became choked up from that short speech and barely kept her lip from trembling. She slipped her arm through Kara’s and clung onto her cut bicep while lifting her lashes to catch a tear on her fingertip. “I feel the same way about you. You have the most amazing qualities in a partner. You exude such positivity from the time you wake up in the morning until you go to sleep at night, and you’re extremely patient with all of us. The same dedication that you give to your work is what you give to our family, and that’s so rare these days. You’ve got this, Kara, and I’ll be standing by your side the whole night.”

     

    The flashing cameras and sea of faces could have unnerved anyone, but Kara squared her jaw and clasped Lena’s hand to lead her from the vehicle. She seemed to draw more strength from Lena’s words and her arrival parted the crowd.

     

    Keeping a lower profile tended to be Kara’s style at big parties, though in this instance she seemed to thrive on the attention and greeted people with waves and smiles.

     

    Lena didn’t expect to stop outside the venue for a photo-op, but when she glanced at her mate, she noticed that Kara wasn’t looking at the cameras.

     

    All of Kara’s attention was on her, and Lena’s heart fluttered in her chest.

     

    “Everyone wanted to coach me for this big moment, you know,” Kara whispered, her eyes fixed on Lena’s like she was the only thing keeping her nerves together. “Cat, Nia, your mother. Heck, even Andrea was giving me tips while I was getting my hair styled, but I told them all I wasn’t going to stop on my way into this place. I didn’t want to feel like an animal being stared at in the zoo, and then I saw you. In this dress.”

     

    Kara exhaled a growl that was lost to the sounds of chatter and yelling as the press called out to them and other attending guests. She slipped her hand a little lower on Lena’s back, and pulled her closer almost by the ass. “I realized I’d be doing the world a disservice if they didn’t get to see how radiant you are tonight, and how proud I am to have you as my mate.”

     

    Of all the product launches and tech events that Lena had attended over the years, not once had her ex flaunted her the way Kara was right then. It thrilled her omega to be put so publicly on display and she blushed as Kara leaned down for a kiss that was destined to be chaste.

     

    Their lips no sooner locked than they had to part again, but the fleeting intimacy left Lena feeling as light as air. She practically floated into the establishment with Kara’s arm about her waist, and leaned into her mate to infuse her senses with calming pheromones.

     

    “Thank you,” Kara muttered, her hand tightening briefly on Lena’s hip to show her gratitude as they surveyed the massive room.

     

    Cat Grant stood smack dab in the middle, surrounded no doubt by investors or potential clients wanting to install the new pool filter.

     

    Lena wasn’t surprised that Kara veered off to the side to postpone introductions for as long as possible. They circled a few waitstaff while Kara quietly asked which ones were the mocktails, and selected two flutes of fruity drinks from the tray. She passed one to Lena with a bright grin, and clinked their glasses together.

     

    “Something tells me I’m going to need a few stronger drinks to get through the night, but I don’t want to embarrass you or myself, so I’ll be sticking to these for a while.” Kara’s mischievous grin widened as she flung her hand up to greet Winn, and he let out a cheer to see them.

     

    “Holy cow, look at you–” Winn laughed, and high fived Kara with enough enthusiasm to sting his own palm. He shook it out as his jaw practically unlatched at the sight of Lena, and then he wordlessly motioned with both hands.

     

    “I know, right? I’m one lucky alpha,” Kara laughed, and puffed herself up like she expected every alpha in the room to be checking Lena out. She cast a glance over Winn’s head with a perplexed crinkle forming between her brows and worried the side of her lip like something was wrong. “Hey, is Brian here yet? He definitely said he was coming, right? I was hoping to introduce him to Lena.”

     

    “This is your elusive friend who helped to create your prototype based on your ideas and the designs you came up with?” Lena asked with a curious lilt that carried in the lift of her chin. She had no idea what Brian looked like, and yet she tried to find him in the crowd.

     

    She spotted a few familiar faces as she scanned the room, and a few unfamiliar people that seemed to be staring.

     

    Sam and Alex were chatting with James and Nia over some canapes, Andrea was rubbing elbows with a few alphas she knew through business, and Lucy was enjoying a glass of champagne with people she obviously met prior to the event.

     

    “Brian is a bit quirky, but one of the nicest people you could ever meet. Just uh—don’t let his first impression fool you,” Winn stated as if in warning, and earned himself a swift whack on the arm from Kara. “What? I’m only trying to help in case he says something weird.”

     

    “Don’t say it like that. He’s socially anxious, not an asshole,” Kara berated under her breath and softened her expression as she turned to Lena. “Ignore what Winn just said. You’re going to get along great with him. If he actually appears.”

     

    Lena raised her brow in a quizzical lift as she spotted an enigmatic, dark-haired individual skulking along in the shadows like a spy. “Is that him over there?”

     

    Sundown hadn’t stopped Brian from wearing a pair of shades to the event. He whipped them off his face as he arrived in front of Kara and complained under his breath, “Kara, they’re serving escargot. I thought we put in a special request for pizza and donuts.”

     

    Winn pulled out a small parchment-lined bag from a bakery, which contained a single frosted donut. “I’ve got your dietary needs covered. Kara, you want one?”

     

    “No—no, I’m good right now,” Kara laughed, faintly blushing and dipping her chin while she seemed to take a second-hand enjoyment from Brian’s antics and his expeditious way of devouring the donut. “I’d like you to finally meet my wi-my Lena.”

     

    “Your Lena is beautiful.” Brian polished off his donut and raised his sunglasses again to blink at Lena in admiration. “The most glamorous omega in attendance by far.”

     

    Lena blushed over his specific wording of compliments and leaned into Kara’s arms. “Kara told me all about you and your brilliant mind. The three of you make the perfect team.”

     

    “They certainly do,” Cat praised in her trademark business tone, strolling over in a custom-embroidered Dior jacket. She tucked her hand into one of the pockets and pulled out a compact-sized device that she gave to Kara. “Norton at the manufacturing company sent this over so we could show off. This is your moment.”

     

    The lights in the grand room suddenly dimmed, and then a bunch of alphas entered in skimpy swimsuits that were designed to look like tuxes. They wheeled in a beautiful and rapidly bubbling fountain, and a spotlight moved onto Cat as she strutted over to it.

     

    Another alpha brought in gallons of sludge, thick and repugnant, and Cat beckoned Kara over to stand at her side.

     

    “Distinguished friends – I wish to present to you a filtration system so powerful and so intelligently designed that I believe it could one day be engineered to clean up our oceans. This is Kara Danvers, the inventor and entrepreneur behind it.” Rather than handle the whole demonstration herself, Cat transferred all of the attention onto Kara with a gesture. The lights moved onto Kara, who stuck out her hand to show off the mini-model.

     

    “This is SAN. It’s smart technology helps isolate pollutants from natural minerals. Where possible, it can even break down those harmful contaminants and restore them to their naturally-occurring basic elements. SAN operates at top speed, ensuring that your water is always crystal clear and safe. I felt that the best way to share its capabilities with you all is to give you a demonstration.” Kara stood tall in explaining her invention, projecting her voice and holding the respect and singular focus of everyone in attendance.

     

    Lena smiled as she realized that SAN not only stood for sanitize but also happened to be an acronym of their daughters’ names – Sophia, Andy, and Natalia. She observed Kara’s demeanor, strength and modesty as she stood back, and allowed her assistants to dump the galloons of sludge into the beautiful fountain.

     

    The flashing lights and bubbling water disappeared under the muck, fading into temporary obscurity until the assistants finished their job.

     

    The whole crowd watched in silence and expectation, murmuring among themselves for the next few minutes as Kara started the filtration device.

     

    “I invite you all to enjoy your drinks and food, and within five minutes, this fountain will be just as beautiful as it was when my helpers wheeled it in,” Cat called out to her rapt audience.

     

    The sophistication of the device was apparent when it fulfilled that promise, and even Lena was taken aback by the speed at which it cleared the fountain.

     

    She knew Kara’s workmanship would be exceptional, though she didn’t ever expect it would be worthy of a global prize as a solution that could help save oceans.

     

    Lena wiped tears of pride from her eyes and hurried over to embrace Kara as soon as she stepped away from the fully-restored fountain.

     

    “I am so proud of you,” Lena breathed and kissed Kara without any care to the observers around them. “So proud to be your mate and so in awe of what you’ve created.”

     

    “I couldn’t have done any of it without you, Lena,” Kara uttered with heartfelt softness.

     

    “As you can see with your own eyes, the power of SAN is revolutionary.” Cat looked impressed as she nodded to Kara and smirked at the frenzy that their brief talk inspired.

     

    For a good hour, they were both swarmed by alphas who wanted to purchase SAN, and Lena was left to sample appetizers with Sam and Alex for company.

     

    “Everything is going to change for Kara from this point onward,” Alex commented, bursting with excitement on her sister’s behalf. “I should have known she would do big things with her life. She slept through calculus, and still had the highest grade in that class.”

     

    “I’m pretty sure this means we can stay at any resort in the world going forward at a great discount because everyone is going to want one of Kara’s devices.” Sam popped the olive from her martini into her mouth and glanced over to where Kara stood surrounded by lots of potential customers.

     

    Lena had never felt the kind of elation she experienced while watching Kara’s glowing face and the animation with which she talked about her product. She ordered a plate of food for Kara and gathered a collection of appetizers to have on hand in case her mate was starved after she finished chatting about business.

     

    The night couldn’t have been more of a success, and it was still early with dancing and several more courses ahead of them.

     

    Lena turned to glance at the large ballroom floor, and that was when she noticed someone entering through the large double doors at the back – an omega in a ravishing jeweled evening gown.

     

    The dark-haired omega parted the crowd as she stepped through it, demure and beautiful as she nodded her thanks to everyone who moved to let her by.

     

    Lena didn’t recognize the guest, and assumed it must have been someone with Cat, since the media mogul was alone and the omega headed in her direction.

     

    It disturbed a tectonic hotspot of emotion inside of Lena when she saw the way Kara whipped around to face the omega. The catastrophic quake inside of Lena must have been apparent on her face, since Sam turned to grab her hand.

     

    “Who is that? Why is Kara looking at her like that?” Sam asked, alarmed and equally stunned by the awe and reverence that registered on Kara’s features.

     

    “Imra,” Alex uttered, sounding both mystified and disdainful by the appearance of the guest. “She’s changed a whole lot. She’s a beta that Kara dated at the end of high school and part way through college. Everyone thought they would end up together. Kara planned most of her dreams around her.”

     

    The information shouldn’t have devastated Lena quite so visibly as it did, and perhaps if she wasn’t so hormonal, it wouldn’t have.

     

    She sucked in a few panicked little breaths as she watched Kara’s jaw uselessly try to form words while she gawked in astonishment at her ex.

     

    Lena recalled the sparse detail that Kara had shared about being heartbroken at the time, but couldn’t bring herself to press Alex for details.

     

    Her mind was still whirring from the fact that even across the room, the faint and mesmerizing scent of an omega in heat definitely came from Imra.

     

    “So what happened, and why is she here?” Sam hissed defensively on Lena’s behalf. She poured a tall glass of water for Lena while she diverted her attention from Alex to glare at the newcomer with inherent distrust and annoyance.

     

    “Kara wouldn’t have invited her. The last I knew, she had blocked Imra across all of her social media accounts years ago,” Alex intoned with her own level of suspicion furrowing her brow. She sucked her teeth as Imra went in for a hug, and Kara belatedly reciprocated, albeit awkwardly as she laughed. “Midway through her first year of college, Imra decided to switch majors and got accepted into one of those fancy colleges in the UK. She expected Kara to just drop everything and join her, but Kara didn’t want to move or delay her own education. State college wasn’t outrageously expensive, but it wasn’t cheap, either, and Kara busted her ass paying for it. As far as I know, Kara was willing to do the whole long distance relationship thing, but Imra wasn’t, and that left Kara with an ultimatum. Go with her, or lose her.”

     

    “Fuck, first loves are brutal,” Sam groaned as she lifted a flute of champagne to down it in one gulp before she turned toward Lena with concerned pheromones. “Are you okay, babe? Do you need a minute? Should I call Kara over?”

     

    “No, but I think I’d like to make introductions,” Lena muttered in distraction with narrowed eyes that took in the flirtatious familiarity Imra displayed.

     

    Imra tried to smooth the lapel of Kara’s tux, though to her mate’s credit, Kara stepped away from the touch and put space between them by grabbing a drink from a passing tray.

     

    Without excusing herself from the table, Lena stood up suddenly and stalked off, consciously concealing the irrational unease and jealousy she felt.

     

    She swept intriguing pheromones around herself like invisible armor, and called to Kara privately through claim pheromones without formally interrupting the conversation first.

     

    The second the commanding scent hit Kara’s nose, she swung her head towards Lena with a bright, infectious smile and held her hand out to usher her over.

     

    That simple act of inclusion eased some of the worry in Lena’s mind, but not enough to loosen the tension she felt in her jaw.

     

    “Lena, there you are. This is Imra.” Kara clasped Lena’s hand to drag her closer the moment their fingers met. “She’s the beta I told you about.”

     

    “Was,” Imra chuckled and used the correction to clasp Kara’s forearm as she smiled up at her through thick, dark lashes. “Of all the mistakes I’ve made through the years, taking evolvents wasn’t one of them.”

    With her delicate facial features, petite stature, and the soft spoken overenunciation of her words, Imra was the epitome of Kara’s type. She carried herself with a calm intensity and gave off sweet and friendly pheromones that were full of apologies.

     

    Kara stood in a hunched posture of distraction, letting her attention wander as if avoidant of dealing with Imra’s remarks. “Yeah—um—what made you decide to do that?”

     

    “Michael. He wanted children.” Imra diverted her eyes temporarily from Kara’s uncomfortable face to the rest of her body language. “Funnily enough, he left me soon after my first heat. Perhaps it was karma for how I foolishly left you for opportunities which led nowhere. It is a gift to be here tonight and to see most of your dreams come true.”

     

    Lena breathed in sharply through her nostrils as she remembered Alex’s earlier words involving Imra’s central role in Kara’s dreams. It irked Lena, but so far, Imra was contrite and honest with Kara, even though her sudden appearance shook up her emotions.

     

    “I’m terribly sorry to bring up the past on a night when you’re celebrating your future,” Imra continued as she held up her personal invitation to the event. “I have to admit I went to lengths to get myself into this room with you. You’re an impossible person to reach, but my sister Preya is close with someone at CatCo and she helped me. I’ve been living back in the states for five years, and I spent all of that time looking for you.”

     

    Kara flinched a little, her eyes twitching shut and her lips falling into a loose line of uncertainty. She normally conveyed her emotions effortlessly with her face, and this was a rare time that she was closed off. Nerves got the better of her, and she clenched and unclenched her hands before blurting out, “I blocked you. I couldn’t stand to see you with someone else. It ate me up inside, and so many of your captions seemed like notes directed at me. I couldn’t handle that kind of emotional torment on a daily basis. I’m sure you came here tonight with the best of intentions, but hopefully you can appreciate that this is all a little overwhelming.”

     

    Being a witness to an intimate dialogue between Kara and anyone else was hard for Lena to emotionally process.

     

    On the one hand, she wanted to be supportive of her mate and protect her from any emotional upheaval that Imra might cause. On the other, she privately harbored a lot of fears about Kara’s outburst, since that meant she still had a lot of unresolved feelings about the situation. Kara might simply have been angry about her ex crashing a party in honor of her and upending her whole night – but there was another possibility, and Kara’s resentments clearly also related to past jealousies over Imra.

    “I do. I do understand that, and that is why I won’t say any more about the subject. I wish for you to enjoy your night, and I’m hopeful that I can leave you with my card, so we can arrange to talk at your convenience. It is a pleasure just to see you again and meet the omega who so captured your heart.”

     

    Imra bowed retiringly and passed over a business card with her personal details on it. She politely nodded to Lena and walked onward to mingle with the other guests.

     

    The emotional whiplash of an ex showing up out of the blue only to walk off again would have been hard for anyone to take, but it was even worse on a night that was meant to be special.

     

    Lena could empathize, given the sheer unsurmountable anguish she had endured while foolishly still holding out for Andrea to love her in a way she deserved.

     

    It had taken an exceptionally long time for them to get to where they were now without animosity and bitterness between them. Kara had played an important role in that, and even Andrea knew it. If not for the fact that Lena had three wonderful children with Andrea, she might never have spoken to her again after finally ending things. So to some degree, Lena understood the frozen look of what the fuck plastered across Kara’s face, even if she hated the sight of it.

     

    Kara expelled all the breath in her lungs with a belated, incredulous laugh that held no humor, and grabbed a flute of champagne to swallow over in one, large gulp. It happened so fast that she was able to place it back on the tray before the waiter moved on, and then she promptly spun towards Lena with wide, wild eyes that conveyed nothing but distress.

     

    “I used to have nightmares like this,” Kara stated in a pitch that wasn’t quite hysterical, but close enough that Lena grasped for her hand to try and comfort her without interrupting. “I’d be somewhere important, completely at ease, and then she would appear out of nowhere like a tiny wrecking ball, and ruin my happiness and everything I’d built without her.
